stories.headline: Trump orders cut in US-South Korea drills after Seoul rejects Iran denuclearisation push
stories.bodyText:
President Donald Trump on Sunday ordered the Pentagon to “substantially” scale back planned joint military exercises with South Korea, citing Seoul’s refusal to join US efforts to “denuclearise” Iran and his relationship with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.
In a post on social media, Trump said the exercises scheduled to begin this week “send a signal that is totally inappropriate and hostile” to North Korea, which he said “has been unthreatening and respectful” during his presidency.
“Therefore, and based on the fact that it is too late to cancel, I have instructed Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth, to substantially reduce the Joint Military Exercises!” Trump wrote.
He added that he had recently asked South Korea's president whether the country wanted to join the US in its efforts to denuclearise Iran, but “they said, ‘No thanks!’”
The 11-day Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises involve about 18,000 South Korean soldiers and are aimed at strengthening the allies' readiness against potential threats from North Korea, AP reported.
North Korea had on Friday condemned the drills as a “rehearsal for an aggressive war” and threatened unspecified countermeasures against the US and South Korea.
The US military has said the exercises are designed to strengthen the alliance and include complex joint operations, including live-fire exercises, precision targeting and manoeuvres, a wet-gap crossing and the distribution of pre-positioned military equipment.
The drills come days after North Korea resumed ballistic missile testing. Earlier this month, South Korea, the US and Japan detected the launch of a short-range ballistic missile from North Korea, its first such test since late June.
Trump hails Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan defence pact
Trump also welcomed the newly signed defence agreement between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan, calling it a “big, bold” first step.
In a post on Truth Social, Trump said, “Very happy to see that Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan have recently, and finally, signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement.”
“It shows how the Middle East is coming together, and how Countries will finally be able to defend themselves in a more meaningful way,” he said.
“This is a big, bold, and important first step — wow!” Trump added.
The trilateral pact, signed at a joint defence summit attended by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, seeks to strengthen security cooperation among the three countries.
According to Pakistan's foreign ministry, the agreement is based on their historical ties, shared strategic interests and longstanding defence cooperation. It includes a commitment that an armed attack against any one of the three countries would be regarded as an attack against all three.

stories.headline: Never accepted Nalsar invitation, so no question of going: CJI
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: 
Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant has not accepted the invitation to be chief guest at the convocation of National Academy of Legal Studies and Research (Nalsar) University of Law amid a row sparked by a section of students opposing his presence at the event which snowballed after Bar Council of India jumped in and ordered blackballing of the graduates before retracting with regret.
Hours after addressing VCs of national law universities at Jodhpur, CJI Kant told TOI he "never consented to Nalsar's invitation" to be chief guest at the convocation.
"The question of me attending the convocation does not arise," CJI said. Four days ago, Nalsar confirmed it had, in keeping with tradition, invited CJI Kant to be chief guest at the ceremony that is likely to be held at the end of Aug or in Sept.
Of Nalsar's 1,400-odd students, more than 400 had opposed CJI Kant as chief guest, citing his remarks during a hearing on petitions related to the students' march to Parliament on July 20 and alleged police excesses.
The CJI-led bench is seized of a bunch of petitions seeking independent inquiry into the alleged police excesses on students, use of pellet guns and facial recognition devices for profiling students in alleged breach of right to privacy.
It has also accepted a petition by the relatives of injured police personnel seeking strict action against "criminal elements" who infiltrated the students' agitation and caused widespread violence and damage to public property while abusing PM and other constitutional functionaries.
The students appeared to have taken umbrage at the CJI-led bench declining to take suo motu cognisance of the alleged police excesses against protesters when an advocate, without filing a proper petition, made the request on July 22, claiming he had video footage of the same. The CJI had asked him to file a proper petition articulating his allegations.
However, when the advocate, without producing a scrap of a paper, persisted with his request that the bench watch the videos, the CJI, with a heavy cache of cases already before him, had asked him not to waste judicial time and suggested he file a proper petition.
Petitions raising similar concerns were subsequently filed and entertained by the CJI-led bench, which had asked police not to take any coercive action against students and preserve all video and CCTV camera footage as well as sought suggestions for an independent inquiry into the incident and setting up a commission to lay down pan-India guidelines for graded action by police to control protests turning violent.

The controversy over students' opposition to the invite to CJI snowballed after BCI chairperson, Manan Kumar Mishra, unilaterally issued a letter to the Nalsar vice-chancellor seeking an inquiry and identification of students who opposed the CJI's presence at the convocation and threatened to debar them from getting registered as advocates.
Faced with condemnation, BCI quickly withdrew the circular. SC has sought its response while observing that the regulator had no business wading into a matter which concerned CJI and Nalsar students.

stories.headline: Trump orders Pentagon to scale back joint exercises with South Korea
stories.deck: U.S. and South Korean forces were set to practise joint operations, but Trump’s comment followed his claim that South Korea refused to help in denuclearising Iran
stories.bodyText:
U.S. President Donald Trump ordered the Pentagon on Sunday (August 16, 2026) to scale back planned joint military exercises with South Korea after he said South Korea declined to help denuclearise Iran.
Mr. Trump said in a social media post that the exercises slated to begin this week are costly and “send a signal that is totally inappropriate and hostile” to North Korea, which he said “has been unthreatening and respectful” while Mr. Trump has been in the White House.
“Therefore, and based on the fact that it is too late to cancel, I have instructed Secretary of War Pete Hegseth to substantially reduce the Joint Military Exercises!” Mr. Trump wrote.
The planned 11-day exercises involving 18,000 South Korean soldiers were designed to beef up readiness against North Korean threats.
U.S. and South Korean forces were expected to practise joint operations in complex scenarios, including a live-fire exercise to test joint precision targeting and manoeuvre, a wet gap crossing, and distribution of prepositioned military equipment, according to the U.S. military.
A day earlier, Mr. Trump posted a photo of himself standing next to North Korea’s Kim Jong Un, writing that the two leaders get along great “despite the unfriendly look in this particular picture”.
North Korea’s Foreign Ministry has called the U.S.-South Korean training “a rehearsal for an aggressive war” that is triggering a different level of instability in the region.
Mr. Trump met with the reclusive North Korean leader three times during his first term to discuss the country’s nuclear programme, most recently in 2019. Since returning to office, Trump has expressed interest in continuing those discussions.
This is not the first time that Mr. Trump has sought to end the exercises. During his first term, he also issued a surprise announcement that called the wargames “provocative”.
“We will be stopping the war games, which will save us a tremendous amount of money, unless and until we see the future negotiation is not going along like it should,” Mr. Trump told reporters after his 2018 meeting with Kim Jong Un in Singapore.

briefs.headline: Fleeing drowning scene not proof of culpability, says SC; acquits 2 held guilty of killing friend
briefs.deck: Acquits 2 Men Held Guilty Of Killing Friend
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Observing that the human mind can sometimes act foolishly, especially in the face of unpredictable adversity, Supreme Court has said that such behaviour cannot be the sole basis of conviction and acquitted two men who had been held guilty of killing their friend.
They were convicted by trial court and high court because their friend drowned in a river in their presence and instead of trying to rescue him, they left the spot and went to watch a movie, actions which were held as evidence of their culpability.
Gujarat high court held that their behaviour was proof that they had killed the friend, and it was not a case of drowning in the river, sentencing them to life imprisonment.
Setting aside the order of trial court and high court, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said there was no evidence to prove that it was a case of murder and held that the deceased had drowned accidentally.
"The accused are guilty of having fled from the spot and not having attempted to rescue the drowning person by crying out for help. Their conduct of having gone for a movie after witnessing their friend drowning, though reprehensible, cannot be found to be an incriminating circumstance, to establish murder rather than drowning. The hypothesis of innocence is crystal clear, and circumstances indicate an accident and not a premeditated murder," the bench said.
Disagreeing with the findings of the HC, the bench said, "We also have to notice the high court's presumption that no person who saw his friend drowning would go to a movie or would take the trouble of bringing back empty soda bottles to the shop from where they purchased it. If such a presumption is accepted then it can be presumed that even after a premeditated murder, the accused would not conduct themselves in that manner."
"The human mind, as has often been held by this court, is at the same time fickle, manipulative and imaginative and the actions, the result of a deprived or a foolish mindset, especially in the face of adversities, cannot be predicted. The subsequent conduct on which the high court found possible the prosecution story of murder rather than of drowning, in this case we are unable to accept. It is the hypothesis of an accidental drowning that looms large from the evidence led at the trial; more plausible than a homicide," SC said.

Challenging their conviction, the accused submitted that they, at worst, could be held guilty of a misadventure which turned fatal for their friend, and there was absolutely no evidence to prove even a homicidal death. They, however, admitted that they fled the scene in panic.

briefs.headline: TMC paid little-known company Rs 160 crore to buy a jet & helicopter: ED
briefs.deck: 'Paid Another Rs 187Cr As Rent But Didn't Utilise Minimum Guaranteed Hours, Chartered Others For Rs 149Cr'
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: An ED investigation into a Kolkata-based aviation company has found that the Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress allegedly funded Rs 160 crore from the party's coffers to a little-known firm, Carewell Aviation India Pvt Ltd, to buy an Embraer jet and an Agusta VIP helicopter, which it subsequently rented out to TMC for Rs 187 crore.
Sources said the money laundering probe was focused on TMC providing an interest-free security deposit of Rs 88.5 crore to the aviation company, which had no funds to buy the jet and the chopper it then gave to the party on rent. As soon as it received the security deposit, Carewell Aviation transferred it to its offshore entity, Carewell Flyjet IFSC Pvt Ltd, registered in Gujarat's Gift City, treated as foreign territory, for further purchase of the jet and the helicopter.
Another fund transfer of over Rs 16 crore from Cayman Island and related to the deal is under investigation.
TMC was required to pay Rs 186.9 crore, exclusive of GST, for using the jet over 72 months and the chopper for 56 months. Although it did not fully utilise the minimum guaranteed flying hours under the charter agreement, the party went on to hire aircraft and helicopters from other companies during this period (2021-26) for a sum of Rs 149 crore, sources said.
When contacted, a TMC source said, "Since the matter is sub judice, we do not want to comment."
The "suspicious" nature of transactions has led ED to delve into the issue of why TMC paid an interest-free security deposit of Rs 88.5 crore when it had to pay charges for renting the aircraft and helicopter. The agreement provided that TMC pay a minimum monthly charge of Rs 90 lakh for the aircraft and Rs 60 lakh for the helicopter.
Carewell Aviation came into being only a few months after TMC returned to office for the third time after the April 2021 assembly elections. Then, after losing the assembly polls in 2026, TMC paid three months advance rental to the company to cover the period till Sept 2026: something that the agency says is contrary to the norm.
Sources said ED has questioned directors of Carewell Aviation over these transactions and recorded their statements on issues such as why it charged TMC Rs 16.5 lakh per flying hour for the jet and when it billed others, who had not helped it with something as crucial as a security deposit, a much lower amount of Rs 7.6 lakh per hour for flying Embraer.
Investigations also showed, sources said, that TMC paid Rs 75 lakh per flying hour to another charter service, Windborne Aviation, for hiring a Falcon 2000 aircraft. TMC used the Falcon aircraft for only about 11-12 flying hours but paid Rs 9.1 crore, which was roughly Rs 75.7 lakh per flying hour.
According to sources, the money trail showed that over Rs 160 crore was transferred to Carewell Aviation and its group entities between July 2021 and June 2026 for "charter services" for the Embraer aircraft and the Agusta chopper. Investigators suspect the transaction to be an "artificial commercial arrangement" and a "calculated device", bereft of any genuine actual financial rationale, considering that the two aircraft were allegedly purchased entirely out of the corpus received from TMC, and the two aviation assets were rented back to the party.
Share your thoughts in the comments
Be respectful · TOI community guidelines
The jet was purchased two months after the charter agreement was signed and security deposit provided. Similarly, the charter agreement for the VIP helicopter was signed by TMC in March 2025 while the chopper was purchased a month later in April.
Carewell Aviation, which was incorporated on Sept 14, 2021, with Pawan Jaju and Ramesh Jaju as its directors, purchased the Embraer Legacy 600 aircraft on June 6, 2023, and the Agusta 109 Grand helicopter on April 17, 2025, using its offshore entity.

stories.headline: Bengaluru celebrates Freedom
stories.deck: Thousands gather for the city’s first-ever Freedom Habba, blending history, culture, music and public participation
stories.bodyText:
As fireworks lit up the sky over Vidhana Soudha on Saturday night, they brought down the curtain on a day Bengaluru had never quite seen before.
Freedom Habba, the city’s first-of-its-kind Independence Day carnival, threw open the grand steps of Vidhana Soudha to citizens from morning to night. Organised by the Karnataka government to mark India’s 80th Independence Day, the festival ran under the theme “Namma Ooru, Nimma Ooru, Nammellara Bengaluru (Our City, Your City, Everyone’s Bengaluru).”
The day opened with a parade of nearly 40 contingents representing different states. A living museum called India’s Freedom Trail recreated key moments from the freedom movement and a Constitution Square featured readings of the Preamble. Children’s activities, game zones, storytelling, arts and crafts, creative workshops, guided tours inside Vidhana Soudha’s Assembly Hall, a 200-foot public art wall and more than 120 ‘Soul Sante’ stalls selling food, crafts and textiles rounded out the afternoon.
The celebrations closed with an evening concert featuring around ten musicians including Raghu Dixit, Sanjith Hegde, Brodha V and M D Pallavi.
Celebrating Bengaluru’s cultural diversity As people from different communities and age groups came together for children’s activities, a history trail and cultural performances, the festival turned into a “microcosm of Bengaluru,” says Ravichandar Venkataraman, civic evangelist and one of the organisers of Freedom Habba.
“The kind of community that came together there was absolutely fantastic. You had people with children, people curious about the Vidhana Soudha tour and its history, another group interested in the evening music and others interested in the state parades,” he shares. “There is a hunger out there among the populace for more of these kinds of outdoor public space activities,” he points out, adding that families are looking for experiences that give children something beyond the usual swing-and-slide activities.
How Gen Z found its way to Freedom Habba
The organisers consciously hoped families with children between six and 14 would attend in large numbers. Social media, QR-based registrations, influencers and collaborations with participating artists were also used to attract younger audiences.
Interestingly, the morning crowds saw families with young children in huge numbers. By late afternoon, that crowd began thinning out as concert-goers arrived. “The morning crowd mostly left soon because those were young kids. They couldn’t stay on till midnight. Then a different set of people came around 4:30 pm to 5 pm for the concert,” Ravichandar says.
Beyond flag-hoisting: A new kind of I-Day  The idea for Freedom Habba, conceived by Chief Minister D K Shivakumar and brought alive by Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda, was to make Independence Day more participatory. “Independence Day should be experienced not just as a ceremony, but as a celebration we create together,” Krishna said, adding that Bengaluru’s mix of cultures, communities and religions makes it a “mini India” and that this diversity was central to the festival.
Ravichandar believes the response to Freedom Habba shows that Bengaluru needs more decentralised cultural events. “How can Koramangala do its own thing, how can Whitefield do its own thing, how can Rajajinagar do its own thing? Once in a while we come up with these central shows, but otherwise you decentralise and get more things done in the neighbourhoods,” he says.
He also expects Freedom Habba to become a regular feature on Bengaluru’s calendar. “I see this becoming a fixture on Bengaluru’s calendar,” he adds, hinting at future editions that could have separate strategies for children’s activities, stalls, and the night concert to better distribute crowds.
Metro curbs disrupt evening commute
The well-coordinated event saw a large number of people making their way to the venue. As footfall increased through the evening, Metro operations and traffic movement around Vidhana Soudha were temporarily affected.
While Dr Ambedkar Metro station was initially announced as closed, restrictions were later extended to stations between MG Road and Nadaprabhu Kempegowda Metro stations until 10:05 pm. Some visitors, particularly families with children and senior citizens, had to walk longer distances or find alternative transport.
Traffic around Vidhana Soudha and connecting roads also slowed as police managed the increased movement of people and vehicles.
What Freedom Habba brought together
- 40 cultural teams paraded traditions from Karnataka and other states.
- India’s Freedom Trail recreated key moments from India’s freedom movement.
- Freedom Wall, a 200-foot public art installation, invited citizens to showcase writing, painting and collaborative artwork.
- Children’s activity zones brought families into the celebration.
- State and district pavilions highlighted India’s diverse cultures and Karnataka’s freedom fighters.
- Freedom Concert brought popular musicians to the Vidhana Soudha steps.
- 22,000-23,000 people were expected to turn out, but the demand was several times higher.

stories.headline: Karnataka bus catches fire, passengers & crew safe
stories.bodyText:
TNN
Gauribidanuru: A 
KSRTC
 bus caught fire near Melya village in Gauribidanuru taluk in Chikkaballapur district Saturday. The incident occurred around 4pm when the bus was heading towards Madipadugu village from Gauribidanuru.
According to Siddalingesh, divisional controller, KSRTC, Chikkaballapur, 32 passengers were on board, and no one was injured. He said the driver noticed a spark in the engine starter and immediately alerted the passengers. The driver and conductor helped the elderly and children get off the bus.
Though the bus was equipped with a fire extinguisher, the crew could not use it as they were busy evacuating the passengers, Siddalingesh said.
A portion of the bus was gutted in the fire. Repairs will be carried out and the bus is expected to return to service within a week, he said.

stories.headline: BMTC adds 62 daily trips on Magadi route with new express service
stories.bodyText:
The Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC) on Sunday introduced a new limited-stop bus service between Magadi Road Toll Gate and Magadi.
The new Vegadootha Vistara service will have 10 buses making 62 trips a day at an interval of 25 minutes. The service commenced on Sunday. The fare has been fixed at ₹55.
The buses will stop at Kamakshipalya, Summanahalli, Sunkadakatte, Gollarahatti, Honaganahatti, Tavarekere, Varadenahalli Handpost and Hospet Circle before reaching Magadi. The fares from Magadi Road Toll Gate range from ₹15 to Kamakshipalya to ₹50 at Hospet Circle.
The BMTC currently operates 33 scheduled services to Magadi, making 190 trips a day. The corporation said the new service was being introduced in response to the strong patronage from commuters travelling to the town.
It is part of the BMTC’s expansion of its limited-stop Vegadootha services connecting Bengaluru with surrounding towns. The corporation currently operates 143 such services across 14 routes to destinations including Attibele, Anekal, Devanahalli, Doddaballapur, Nelamangala, Dobspet, Bidadi, Harohalli and Hoskote.

stories.headline: Yakshagana, Dhol Tasha, Garba add colour to Bengaluru’s first Freedom Habba
stories.deck: People from diverse communities, States and districts dressed in traditional attire showcased their folk traditions, culture, music and dance
stories.bodyText:
For the first time, Bengaluru celebrated Independence Day by hosting Freedom Habba in front of the grand steps of Vidhana Soudha on Saturday. Organised by the Karnataka government the event was a first-of-a-kind, citizen-led festival.
There were people from diverse communities, States and districts who were dressed in traditional attire to showcase their folk traditions, culture, music and dance. From Karnataka’s Yakshagana, Veeragaase to Hulivesha, Maharashtra’s dhol tasha, Gujarati Garba , to West Bengal’s Dhanuchi Naach, Sikh traditional martial arts including Chakkar bazi and Gatka, various forms of art were exhibited.
Atleast 30 such teams paraded their art and skills for nearly half a kilometer. At the end of the parade, each team went on the stage set at the entrance of Vidhana Soudha and explained the importance of their art, culture and traditions.
Amit J, a degree student from Government Arts College in Bengaluru who was at the celebrations, said, “Our team is called Kalamilana. When we got a call from the representatives of the government, we were happy to participate and showcase Yakshagana. .”
Meanwhile, Kuntur Kumara team had travelled from Malavalli in Mandya district to perform Puje Kunitha. Explaining the art form, he said, “Dancers balance heavy, decorated structures with colourful silk cloth and flowers on their heads and do acrobatic movements. Puje Kunitha is performed during grama devathe’s worship or festival in villages. It is mostly performed in Mandya district, Mysuru, Ramanagara and Channapattana.”
Besides the parade, an immersive living museum called India’s Freedom Trail showcased information on Salt Satyagraha, Quit India Movement, while district themed pavilions showcased contributions of Sangolli Rayanna, Rani Chennamma to highlight Karnataka’s contribution to India’s freedom struggle. There were also a Constitution square, children’s games and activity zones.
Vaishnavi R, a visitor at the Freedom Habba, said, “I had never seen Vidhana Soudha so close. I had booked a guided tour in which all the important spots inside Soudha, a replica of Vidhana Soudha made of sandalwood, wood carvings and the meaning behind it were explained. Later, I walked out to be part of the Freedom Habba. Being a Bengalurean, I am celebrating Independence day in a unique way.”
Confusion among metro commuters, park visitors
As the Cubbon Park started closing at 6 p.m., visitors to the park were left confused about the exit route from the park. While they tried to exit from roads close to High Court and B R Ambedkar Metro Station, police personnel directed them towards other alternative routes like BSNL Gate, Bal Bhavan Gate and the gate near Century club.
Police personnel ensured that only those with registered QR codes were going for the habba and allowed entry near GPO office, BSNL gate and MS building.
The screening process created bottlenecks for people not attending the festival. In one instance, an elderly man was stopped by the police despite repeatedly explaining that he was merely heading to Shivajinagar and not the event. Finally, he was allowed to exit.
Meanwhile, Namma metro services were stopped at Cubbon Park, Sir M Visvesvaraya Metro stations and Vidhana Soudha metro stations for sometime and commuters were allowed to get down at MG Road and Nadaprabhu Kempegowda Metro Stations until 9.30 p.m. Services resumed once the programme ended.

briefs.headline: JD(S) functionary assaults traffic cop on duty in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A traffic police constable was allegedly assaulted while on duty at Gottigere after a man identified as Manjunath alias Gottigere Manjanna, JD(S) state general secretary, objected to his vehicle being stopped by traffic police Sunday evening.
The incident occurred around 4pm when constable Arun, attached to Hulimavu traffic police station, was regulating traffic at Gottigere, a few metres from the station. He stopped Manjanna’s vehicle using a hand signal to allow vehicles travelling in the opposite direction to pass.
According to the complaint, Manjanna questioned the constable about stopping his vehicle. During the argument, he allegedly tried to assault him, grabbed him by the collar and attempted to attack him with the help of his aide.
A Hulimavu traffic officer said that after the incident, Manjanna called a senior police officer and complained about the constable stopping his vehicle. A mobile phone video that has gone viral shows Manjanna, while speaking to the officer, allegedly attempting to kick the constable.
Later, the constable was allegedly made to apologise to Manjanna. However, the move by senior officers did not go down well with junior police personnel. 
The situation soon escalated, prompting members of the public and Hulimavu traffic police to intervene and separate the two.
Deputy commissioner of police (South-Traffic) said, “By the time the incident came to our notice, the constable had gone home. We have called him back to enquire about the incident.”
Joint commissioner of police (East) Ramesh Banoth said a case had been registered at Hulimavu police station in connection with the incident and an investigation was under way.
Another senior officer said the case was registered under charges of assault or criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging his duty, along with other appropriate sections.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru Metro expresses regret over ‘Freedom Habba’ chaos
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: The Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd (BMRCL) Sunday expressed regret over the temporary suspension of train stoppages at two stations in central Bengaluru during the ‘Freedom Hubba’ celebrations Saturday, saying the measures were taken in the interest of passenger safety.
“BMRCL sincerely regrets the inconvenience experienced by passengers during this period. We understand that any unexpected change in metro operations can cause considerable difficulty to commuters and disrupt their planned journeys,” the metro operator said.
BMRCL had announced in advance that the Dr BR Ambedkar (Vidhana Soudha) Metro station would remain closed for passenger entry and exit from 10am Saturday as part of crowd-management arrangements for the event.
However, by evening, exceptionally heavy pedestrian movement in and around Vidhana Soudha, coupled with a significant rise in passenger footfall at Cubbon Park and Sir M Visvesvaraya Metro Stations, led to rapid crowd build-up at the stations and their approaches.
“Considering the prevailing crowd situation and in the interest of public safety, train stoppages at Cubbon Park and Sir M Visvesvaraya Metro stations were temporarily implemented between 7.21pm and 9.57pm, in consultation with the competent authorities responsible for traffic and crowd management at the event,” BMRCL said.
The temporary measure affected thousands of commuters who had relied on the Metro to reach or leave the Vidhana Soudha area.
BMRCL said train capacity and crowd conditions outside stations have to be managed together during large public gatherings. “When the surrounding roads and station approaches became heavily congested, the temporary non-stoppage at these two stations was necessary to regulate further inflow into the area and facilitate safe dispersal of the crowd already present,” it said.
As the situation improved, Cubbon Park and Sir M Visvesvaraya Metro Stations resumed normal operations at 9:57pm. The Dr BR Ambedkar (Vidhana Soudha) station reopened for passenger operations after 10.05pm.
BMRCL said the experience from Saturday’s event would be factored into planning for future large gatherings in coordination with the concerned authorities.
It said particular attention would be given to advance assessment of passenger flows, crowd management, deployment of additional personnel and timely communication of operational changes to commuters.

briefs.headline: Onam rush in Bengaluru: Vande Bharat coaches doubled for Ernakulam
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Helping passengers tackle the 
Onam
 travel rush, 
Southern Railway
 (SR) has doubled the coaches on the KSR Bengaluru-Ernakulam Junction Vande Bharat Express. From Monday, the train will run with 16 coaches in both directions, six days a week.
Passengers travelling to 
Kerala
 from Bengaluru had been demanding increased capacity for months. Till Sunday, the train operated with just eight coaches despite strong demand and long waiting lists.
Train Nos. 26651/26652 will now accommodate more passengers between KSR Bengaluru and Ernakulam. South Western Railway (SWR) said the augmentation will double the train’s capacity from eight to 16 coaches, improving travel convenience on the Bengaluru-Kerala route.
The Vande Bharat is the most popular such service from Bengaluru, but its limited capacity led to heavy waiting lists. With Onam beginning next week, tickets had sold out nearly two months in advance.
According to SWR data, the KSR Bengaluru service recorded the highest booking rate among Vande Bharat trains in Karnataka at 141% in 2025-26. Since its launch in Nov 2025, it has carried over 90,000 passengers and earned the railways Rs 11.1 crore.
Reji Kumar, general secretary, Kerala Samajam Bangalore, said the demand for more coaches had been raised since the beginning of the year. “We welcome this move from the ministry as it will be very helpful for the huge Malayali community living in Bengaluru to reach their homes for Onam. It was very difficult to get tickets earlier; now the situation might be eased,” he said.

briefs.headline: Four years on, Bengaluru’s airport-model railway terminal struggles with ticket chaos, poor upkeep
briefs.deck: TOI Reality Check
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Just two months ago, Sir M Visvesvaraya Terminal (SMVT) at Byappanahalli completed its fourth year. India’s first fully air-conditioned railway terminal with airport-like infrastructure now paints a different picture of neglect and poor enforcement.
Despite assurances from South Western Railway (SWR), passenger amenities at the high-budget terminal have seen little improvement. A reality check conducted by TOI Thursday night revealed severe operational gaps at the station, which handles thousands of long-distance commuters daily.
During peak hours, when multiple long-distance trains were scheduled to depart, ticket counters were found shut. Passengers—a significant portion of whom were migrant workers—were forced to rely on just three automatic ticket vending machines (ATVMs), which proved woefully inadequate for the surge. No ATVM facilitators were present to assist them.
Amid the confusion, a Railway Protection Force (RPF) officer was heard announcing via a body-worn microphone: “Whoever wants to go to Guwahati, the train is overcrowded, no more unreserved tickets will be sold.” As anxious passengers crowded around asking where they could buy tickets, the officer later announced that tickets were only available for a Mysuru-bound train.
Commuters looking for guidance found no information center or help desk outside the terminal building. Entry into the glass-walled terminal is strictly regulated via platform or journey tickets, which can only be bought outside. While an official help desk exists in the central concourse inside, no staff was present to address queries during the night.
Crowds swell, amenities shrink at Bengaluru’s SMVT
SWR denied a technical glitch at the ticket counters. “Yesterday night, based on the number of general tickets already issued for train No. 12509, Guwahati Express, further sale of general tickets for this train through the counters was temporarily stopped to avoid overcrowding in the coaches. Passengers were also informed about the next available train to their respective destinations.”, an official said.
Passengers sleep on floor
By 10:30pm, the station concourse and external corridors transformed into a makeshift dormitory. Over 100 passengers—including women, children, and youth—were seen sleeping on the granite floor inside and outside the terminal building.
While SMVT features a dedicated air-conditioned sleeping zone, several slots remained empty Thursday night. Operators stated that the minimum package starts at Rs 500, a fee far out of reach for daily-wage migrant workers who form a major chunk of the station’s footfall.
Furthermore, despite SWR’s earlier claims that the central air-conditioning system is fully functional and continuously monitored, passengers inside the enclosed terminal were seen sweating, with the open platforms offering cooler air than the concourse.
Spiking footfall, slow upkeep
In May, when 
TOI
 reported on the poor upkeep of the station, SWR responded that continuous efforts were being made to enhance passenger amenities. Despite assurances, the situation remains similar to what it was three months later.
SWR clarified that a new booking office with ticket counters, along with separate waiting halls for men and women, retiring rooms, and dormitories, has been sanctioned at a cost of Rs 17.1 crore, and the works are in progress.
The station remains crucial for passengers as it generates significantly high footfall. Daily average footfall here rose from 11,691 in 2022-23 to 36,022 in 2025–26.

briefs.headline: Man, 72, falls from 18th floor in Bengaluru, dies
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A 72-year-old man died after falling from the 18th floor of an apartment building on Magadi Road Sunday afternoon. Police are yet to ascertain if it was an accidental fall or suicide.
The deceased is Paramaeshwaraiah, who lived with his wife, children and grandson in the apartment.
Police said Paramaeshwaraiah fell from the 18th floor, sustained severe injuries and died on the spot. The security guards and a few residents, who heard a huge noise, rushed towards the spot and found him dead in a pool of blood. A police officer said a chair had been placed on the balcony, and Paramaeshwaraiah is suspected to have climbed onto it before falling. “The family told us the chair had been kept there for cleaning. We are yet to ascertain whether he jumped or fell accidentally,” the officer said.
Based on a complaint from the family, police have registered a case of unnatural death at KR Agrahara police station and are investigating. The body has been kept at the mortuary, and a postmortem will be conducted on Monday.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru’s woman SI assaulted, body-shamed while trying to break up quarrel
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:  A woman police sub-inspector was allegedly abused, manhandled and body-shamed while trying to break up a quarrel involving a lawyer and a police constable at Bhattarahalli signal recently.
KR Pura police have registered a case based on her complaint against a lawyer, his friend, a student, the lawyer’s father and others.
According to the woman sub-inspector’s complaint, she was on duty on Old Madras Road near Bhattarahalli signal around 8.40am on Aug 12 when she found a scooterist arguing with traffic constable Manjunath after being stopped for riding on the wrong side of a one-way road. When she intervened and questioned him, the scooterist identified himself as a lawyer and allegedly picked a quarrel with her. He allegedly grabbed her hands, dragged her while she was in uniform and assaulted her.
Her subordinates, a constable and an assistant sub-inspector who were on duty at the signal, reportedly intervened and tried to stop the altercation. However, the advocate allegedly continued abusing the woman sub-inspector and called his friend, a student, to the spot.
The friend allegedly told the woman sub-inspector that he was a student and that she could not take any action against him. 
He also allegedly grabbed and pulled her right hand, injuring her finger. The sub-inspector said she pushed him away in self-defence, held his shirt and asked her subordinates to call the 112 helpline.
The situation escalated when the lawyer’s brother, father and others arrived at the spot. The lawyer’s father allegedly made derogatory remarks about the woman sub-inspector’s body, comparing her to a buffalo, while his brother allegedly made threatening and abusive comments.
The advocate allegedly threatened to get her removed from service and warned that he would photograph and record her and circulate the visuals on social and mainstream media.
The commotion was brought under control after members of the public and police personnel intervened. The woman sub-inspector later informed the control room and senior police officers about the incident.
She later sought treatment at KR Pura government hospital and filed a complaint. She said the confrontation began after the lawyer allegedly violated traffic rules and obstructed traffic, leading to an argument with a car driver. The dispute caused congestion, prompting the driver to alert constable Manjunath.
When Manjunath asked the lawyer to move his vehicle and clear the road, the argument escalated. The woman sub-inspector intervened but was allegedly abused, assaulted and threatened while on duty in uniform. The incident was captured on the traffic police body camera.
Counter-complaint for assault
A senior officer said the lawyer’s friend, a student, has filed a counter-complaint accusing the woman sub-inspector of assaulting him and damaging his mobile phone. A video of the incident went viral Sunday evening, in which the student claimed he had intervened when the advocate and a car driver were fighting and was allegedly assaulted by the woman sub-inspector when he questioned them.
Police have registered a non-cognisable report (NCR) and are seeking court permission to register an FIR. Notices have been served on the accused and an investigation is under way.

briefs.headline: ‘Protect farmers, abide by law’: Karnataka CM Shivakumar on releasing Cauvery water to TN
briefs.deck: Karnataka faces challenges protecting farmers and releasing Cauvery water. The state government seeks good rainfall to ease water availability issues. Karnataka will challenge the Cauvery Water Management Authority's release order. The Mekedatu project remains a point of discussion with Tamil Nadu. New legislation on public property use aims to clarify existing rules.
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Karnataka chief minister D K Shivakumar on Sunday said the state faces a dual challenge of protecting farmers’ livelihoods while complying with legal directions on releasing Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu, and called for good rainfall to help overcome the situation.
Speaking to the media after visiting a temple at Bhagamandala in Kodagu district, Shivakumar said the government must balance the needs of farmers with its legal obligations on water sharing.
"Our dams have not filled yet. We have two big challenges: Releasing water to Tamil Nadu, abiding by the law, and protecting our farmers. Certainly we will protect the interests of our farmers. It is my duty too," Shivakumar said.
He said the government had a responsibility to ensure water for drinking and agriculture and that the availability of water in reservoirs would determine how much could be released for irrigation.
"Depending on the availability of water at dams, we have to release it to farmers for their crops. Our wish is that there should be good rainfall, crops should flourish, and farmers should have food and livelihood," he added.
On the Mekedatu project, Shivakumar said Karnataka would continue to protect its interests. He noted that the Supreme Court had stated that there was no objection to constructing a dam within the state and said the Centre had also conveyed a similar position in Parliament while responding to a question from a Tamil Nadu MP.
Mekedatu is a proposed multi-purpose project for drinking water and power, involving the construction of a balancing reservoir near Kanakapura in Bengaluru South district. Tamil Nadu has opposed the project, arguing that it could affect the state’s water supply.
Shivakumar reiterated that the project would not affect Tamil Nadu’s allocated share of 177.25 TMC of Cauvery water and said separate formulas were in place for water sharing during distress years.
The Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC), which met in New Delhi last Tuesday, directed Karnataka to release 12,000 cusecs of water per day to Tamil Nadu from August 12 for 15 days. The Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) later upheld the order.
The Karnataka government has decided to challenge the CWMA’s order in the Supreme Court.
Referring to the water-sharing dispute, Shivakumar said Karnataka must protect both its farmers and its legal obligations.
The Cauvery Water Management Authority has issued certain directions. "If there is any crisis, a situation may come where we may have to give the dam keys to the Centre. That should not happen. We have to protect the livelihood of our farmers and also protect and abide by the law. This is very important. To overcome all these, we need blessings of rain gods and all of us should pray for them," he said.
On proposed law governing use of public property
Shivakumar also responded to BJP national general secretary B L Santosh’s reported remarks that the RSS would not register under the state government’s proposed Bill concerning unauthorised use of public property.
He said there was no reason for the RSS or Santosh to be concerned and maintained that the proposed legislation was not directed at any particular organisation.
"We don't want to hurt anyone's feelings. Whichever religion or organisation, they must follow law... If an organisation submits an application seeking permission from the government, the necessary permission and staff arrangements will be provided according to the rules," he said.
Responding to Santosh’s remarks, Shivakumar said, "He is a senior leader. Let us also listen to his guidance. We have only provided greater clarity regarding the provisions that already exist in the law. Nobody needs to panic."
He cited the example of Minister Krishna Byre Gowda obtaining government permission to hold the "Freedom Habba" programme in front of Vidhana Soudha on Saturday.
The chief minister said political parties and other organisations, including the JD(S), BJP and Congress, could hold programmes as long as they followed the law.

briefs.headline: I-Day: CM announces new schemes to boost job creation, AI push in education
briefs.deck: Chief Minister announces Karnataka targets one lakh new jobs through Udyoga Sankalpa and Udyoga Nidhi schemes, creation of AI hubs, and a $3 trillion economy by 2047
briefs.bodyText:
Karnataka will focus on creating one lakh new jobs, expanding artificial intelligence (AI) education, and establishing technology hubs across the State as part of its vision for a “Young Karnataka–New India”, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said on August 15.
In his first Independence-Day address after taking over as Chief Minister, at Manekshaw Parade Ground in Bengaluru, Mr Shivakumar announced the launch of the Chief Minister Udyoga Sankalpa and Udyoga Nidhi schemes, aimed at improving employment opportunities and encouraging job creation.
The State Government has begun the process of filling 72,000 key vacancies, with notifications for all the posts expected to be issued within the next six months, he said.
Under Udyoga Nidhi, entrepreneurs in 10 economically backward districts will receive an incentive of ₹2,500 per month for every new job created, with the government targeting one lakh additional jobs through the initiative.
AI from class 6 in govt schools
The Chief Minister outlined an ambitious technology and education agenda. AI will be introduced in government schools from class 6, alongside the proposed AI Akshara Abhiyana and Coding Gurukula programmes. Bengaluru will get the country’s first government-owned AI university, while AI hubs will be established to strengthen the State’s technology ecosystem.
Under the ‘Beyond Bengaluru’ initiative, five global technology centres are proposed in Kalaburagi, Belagavi, Hubballi-Dharwad, Mangaluru and Mysuru. An Advanced Manufacturing Cluster is being established in Doddaballapura, with investment commitments of ₹20,000 crore and an expected employment potential of around one lakh jobs.
Mr. Shivakumar said, “Karnataka is targeting a $3 trillion economy, equivalent to ₹320 lakh crore, by 2047. The State’s per capita income had reached ₹4.33 lakh, and Karnataka ranked second in GST and income-tax collections.”
Calling on people of Karnataka to participate in the State’s development, Mr. Shivakumar said, “Two hands alone are not enough to pull the chariot of the State’s development. The hands of every Kannadiga must join mine. Let us come together and pull the chariot of development.”
The government plans to integrate technology into agriculture through the Chief Minister Raitha Chaitanya scheme, under which drones and satellite imagery will be used for crop surveys. The Raitha Mitra scheme will provide farmers owning three acres or less with a 50% subsidy on agricultural machinery rental charges.
On infrastructure, Mr. Shivakumar said, “1,663 km of State Highways, 3,000 km of major district roads, and 125 bridges had been constructed over the past year. Development of 7,100 km of rural roads is under way under the Pragathi Patha scheme with an investment of ₹5,200 crore.”
For Bengaluru, infrastructure projects worth ₹1.50 lakh crore have been taken up. The Namma Metro network is expected to expand to 220 km after completion of Phase III, while a 117-km ring road under the Bengaluru Business Corridor is planned at a cost of ₹26,000 crore, he said.
According to the Chief Minister, the government has prioritised water security, with 112 major water-resource projects worth ₹16,000 crore approved this year. The first phase of the Yettinahole Integrated Drinking Water Project is nearing completion, with water expected to reach Tumakuru district by November.
Highlighting the government’s welfare measures, he said that ₹77,000 crore had so far been transferred directly to 1.28 crore women under the Gruha Lakshmi scheme, while 1.65 crore households were receiving free electricity under Gruha Jyothi. Women in Karnataka had made around 796 crore free journeys under the Shakti scheme.
Karnataka to set up state-run motor vehicle insurance corporation
Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar has announced a proposal to create a state-owned Motor Vehicle Insurance Corporation aimed at making insurance services more accessible to vehicle owners.
Speaking during his Independence Day address, Mr Shivakumar said that escalating insurance costs and difficulties in securing compensation after accidents have placed a growing burden on families. The proposed corporation is expected to simplify documentation, improve price transparency and speed up claim settlements, potentially offering an alternative to private insurers.
However, details regarding the corporation’s structure, insurance premiums and coverage are yet to be finalised.
CM announces dividing Bengaluru Police Commissionerate into five units
Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, in his Independence Day address on Saturday, announced plans to reorganise Bengaluru’s police administration by dividing the existing commissionerate into five units.
“The Greater Bengaluru Authority and five municipal corporations have been established to improve governance and public safety. As part of the restructuring, the Bengaluru police commissionerate will also be reorganised into five separate commissionerates,” he said.
The Hindu had reported on the plan, with sources mentioning that the proposed commissionerates will cover Central, East, West, North and South Bengaluru along the lines of the new civic corporations. Each unit is expected to have two to four law-and-order divisions and one to two traffic divisions, headed by Deputy Commissioners of Police.
Guarantee scheme figures don’t match, says BJP
Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly R. Ashok on Saturday demanded that the Karnataka government issue a white paper on the implementation and expenditure of its guarantee schemes, alleging discrepancies in figures presented by different government sources.
Referring to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar’s Independence Day speech, Mr. Ashok said the figures cited for the Shakti scheme did not match those previously released by the government. “The Chief Minister said 796 crore free journeys had been undertaken by women, with ₹14,875 crore spent over three years. However, earlier government posts had cited 753.7 crore journeys and ₹19,771 crore in expenditure,” he said.
He also pointed to discrepancies in Gruhalakshmi figures. “While the Chief Minister said ₹76,908 crore had been disbursed to 1.28 crore beneficiaries, earlier figures put the amount at ₹74,216 crore for 1.24 crore women,”he added.

stories.headline: FPIs turn buyers again, pump Rs 16,621 crore into Indian equities in August
stories.deck: In August, foreign investors turned the tide by purchasing Indian equities, building on the positive momentum from July's inflows. This shift follows a period of substantial selling earlier in the year. With attractive valuations and promising corporate earnings, renewed interest from foreign investors is evident, particularly in the domestic consumption sectors such as healthcare and consumer…
stories.bodyText:
Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) turned buyers of Indian equities once again in August, pouring in Rs 16,621 crore during the first fortnight of the month. The buying comes amid improving relative valuations, resilient corporate earnings and growing expectations of lower interest rates in the US.
The latest investment adds to the Rs 20,200 crore that foreign investors poured into Indian equities in July. The two months of buying mark a reversal from the heavy selling seen earlier in the year.
FPIs had been on a four-month selling streak before July, pulling out Rs 49,340 crore in June, Rs 32,963 crore in May, Rs 60,847 crore in April and Rs 1.17 lakh crore in March. They had invested Rs 22,615 crore in February before the selling began, CDSL data showed.
Even with the recent turnaround, foreign investors remain net sellers for 2026. Their withdrawals from Indian equities have reached around Rs 2.4 lakh crore so far this year, already higher than the Rs 1.66 lakh crore they pulled out over the entire 2025.
Experts said the change in sentiment reflects a mix of factors that have made Indian equities more attractive to foreign investors. These include valuations compared with other markets, steady corporate earnings, expectations of US rate cuts, softer crude prices and reduced currency volatility.
"The key drivers are improving relative valuations, resilient corporate earnings, expectations of softer US rates, lower currency volatility and some diversification away from crowded Korea-Taiwan AI trades. AI became a magnet of all capital across the world," Manish Bhandari, CEO and portfolio manager, Vallum Capital told PTI.
The earlier FPI selling was more closely linked to global macroeconomic factors than concerns specific to India, said Vedant Gupte, Co-Founder and CEO of investment platform Trackk.
"Expectations of US rate cuts, softer crude and a rupee that has stopped misbehaving have removed the three reasons foreign investors had to stay away," Gupte said.
The buying pattern has also become more selective, with foreign investors increasingly looking towards sectors connected with domestic consumption, according to Gupte.
"Consumer durables and healthcare are attracting interest. Foreign investors are underwriting the Indian household, not the Indian invoice," he said.
July's sectoral data reflected this preference, with Consumer Services, Healthcare, Consumer Durables, Metals & Mining and IT recording strong FPI buying. Several other sectors, however, continued to see net selling.
The recent buying trend could remain vulnerable to shifts in global market conditions. Foreign investor flows are expected to remain sensitive to US treasury yields, the dollar index, crude oil prices and changes in corporate earnings expectations.
Crude oil prices and developments related to the ongoing US-Iran geopolitical tensions will be among the key factors investors track in the coming week, said Pabitro Mukherjee, deputy vice president-research at Bajaj Broking.
Foreign investors have also continued to put money into debt. During the period under review, FPIs invested Rs 972 crore through the Fully Accessible Route (FAR), while another Rs 69 crore flowed through the general route.

stories.headline: Rs 6,400-crore IPO rush: 7 companies set to tap primary market next week
stories.deck: The IPO market anticipates a busy week with seven companies planning public offerings. These upcoming issues aim to collectively raise more than Rs 6,400 crore from investors. Horizon Industrial Parks and Lalithaa Jewellery Mart will launch their initial public offerings on August 17. Shankesh Jewellers and Sunshine Pictures are scheduled to open their issues on August 18.
stories.bodyText:
The IPO market is heading into another packed week, with seven companies scheduled to come out with public issues between August 17 and 21, seeking to raise more than Rs 6,400 crore collectively.
The line-up includes Horizon Industrial Parks, backed by Blackstone, jewellery retailer Lalithaa Jewellery Mart, Shankesh Jewellers, Sunshine Pictures, Gaja Alternative Asset Management, Tempsens Instruments and Augmont Enterprises.
The fresh batch of issues comes after five IPOs were launched this week and three companies had already entered the market earlier this month. With the seven upcoming offerings, the number of companies launching IPOs in 2026 is expected to reach 55, industry data showed.
Horizon, Lalithaa to open IPOs on August 17
Horizon Industrial Parks and Lalithaa Jewellery Mart will be the first to hit the market, with both IPOs opening on August 17. Horizon is looking to raise Rs 2,600 crore, while Lalithaa Jewellery Mart has set the issue size at Rs 1,700 crore.
Horizon Industrial Parks' IPO is entirely a fresh issue and carries a price band of Rs 57-60 per share. The company intends to use the proceeds to repay borrowings.
Lalithaa Jewellery Mart has fixed the price band at Rs 190-201 per share. 
Its offering consists of a fresh issue of up to Rs 1,200 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to Rs 500 crore.
Shankesh Jewellers, Sunshine Pictures next in line
The primary market will see two more issues open on August 18. Shankesh Jewellers will seek to raise Rs 367 crore, while Sunshine Pictures will raise Rs 282 crore.
Shankesh Jewellers has set a price band of Rs 88-93 per share. Its IPO comprises a fresh issue of up to 2.95 crore equity shares and an OFS of up to 1 crore equity shares.
Sunshine Pictures has fixed its price band at Rs 342-360. Its Rs 282-crore issue comprises a fresh issue of 48 lakh equity shares and an OFS of 30.37 lakh equity shares, taking the total offer size to 78.37 lakh shares. Promoters Vipul Amrutlal Shah and Shefali Vipul Shah will sell shares through the OFS.
Gaja Capital, Tempsens follow
Gaja Alternative Asset Management, which operates under the Gaja Capital brand, will open its Rs 550-crore IPO on August 19. The company has set a price band of Rs 152-160 per share. The issue comprises a fresh issue of up to Rs 450 crore and an OFS of up to Rs 100 crore.
Tempsens Instruments will follow on August 20 with a fresh issue of Rs 95 crore and an OFS of 1.85 crore shares. The company is yet to announce the price band, which will be disclosed on Monday.
Augmont to close week's IPO calendar
The week's IPO calendar will close with Augmont Enterprises on August 21. The integrated gold and silver platform will raise Rs 825 crore through a combination of a Rs 620-crore fresh issue and an OFS of Rs 205 crore. Its price band will be announced on Tuesday.
The proceeds from the fresh issues are expected to be used largely for business expansion, capital expenditure, debt repayment and other corporate purposes, while the money raised through OFS will accrue to the selling shareholders.
The IPO pipeline will remain active even after these seven offerings, with air freight forwarding and logistics company Skyways Air Services scheduled to launch its Rs 583-crore issue on August 24.

stories.headline: ONGC gets U.S. licence to resume full Venezuela operations, eyes operatorship
stories.deck: The U.S. approval removes a key hurdle for ONGC's Venezuelan investments and could pave the way for the state-run explorer to expand production
stories.bodyText:
State-owned Oil and Natural Gas Corp (ONGC) has secured a licence from the U.S. Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), allowing it to resume full operations in Venezuela after years of limiting activity because of sanctions-related risks, a senior company official said.
The U.S. approval removes a key hurdle for ONGC's Venezuelan investments and could pave the way for the state-run explorer to expand production, sign new agreements and take over operatorship of some projects from Venezuela's state oil company PDVSA, Anupam Agarwal, director-finance at ONGC, said at an investor call post first quarter earnings announcement.
"Now we have full freedom to work on the Venezuela project because earlier we were restricting our operations there because of the sanction-related risks. Those risks are behind us," Mr. Agarwal said.
ONGC Videsh Ltd, the company's overseas investment arm, holds a 40% interest in the San Cristobal oil project, while the remaining is with Venezuela's Petroleos de Venezuela S.A. (PDVSA).
It holds another 11% stake in the Carabobo project, which is under development.
An OFAC license would enable the company to manage the finances of its Venezuelan projects and help it recover a pending dividend of more than $500 million.
ONGC is already in talks with Venezuelan authorities and its joint-venture partners over its interests in two projects, San Cristobal and Carabobo, and expects positive developments soon, including new agreements and a possible transfer of operatorship from PDVSA, he said.
The licence is significant for ONGC because U.S. sanctions on Venezuela's oil sector have for years complicated financial transactions, investment and operations involving Venezuelan crude and energy assets. The company had therefore curtailed activity despite its longstanding presence in the country.
The company can now invest in the projects to raise oil production. San Cristobal produced around 0.265 million tonnes of oil equivalent in FY26. This is a 10th of the production potential, and the OFAC license means it can invest in raising output.
Venezuela’s strategic importance
Venezuela is strategically important for ONGC because it holds the world's largest proven crude oil reserves, estimated by OPEC at about 303 billion barrels, more than Saudi Arabia. Much of the country's production potential remains constrained by years of underinvestment, sanctions and operational difficulties, leaving substantial scope for additional development.
Mr. Agarwal said Venezuela's newly enacted petroleum law provides additional fiscal incentives for resource development, potentially improving the investment environment for foreign oil companies and their local partners.
“ONGC's focus is on shallow, onshore fields in Venezuela, where it has relevant operating expertise from its domestic fields in Western India, including Mehsana and Ahmedabad,” Mr. Agarwal said.
The company sees the projects as a natural fit with its existing capabilities and is now seeking to accelerate development after the easing of sanctions-related constraints.
"We are very bullish for Venezuela," Mr. Agarwal said, adding that ONGC expects to see new agreements and potentially take over operatorship of some projects from PDVSA in the near term.
OVL invested in Venezuelan oil assets through joint ventures, but sanctions imposed by Washington on Venezuela's oil sector have periodically restricted the scope of operations and dealings with PDVSA.
The renewed push into Venezuela comes as India seeks to secure overseas oil resources and diversify its supply base amid heightened geopolitical risks.
For ONGC, greater operational control over Venezuelan fields could also give the company a larger role in unlocking some of the world's biggest undeveloped and underproduced hydrocarbon resources.

stories.headline: ONGC expects oil plus gas production of 39 MMTOE this fiscal, 40 MMTOE next year
stories.deck: In the analyst call, senior executive of ONGC stated they expect oil prices to hover at about $75 per barrel, which would also make it ideal to pursue deepwater exploration
stories.bodyText:
Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) expects cumulative oil plus gas production to scale 39 million metric tonnes (MMT) in the ongoing fiscal and 40 MMT in FY 2028, Anupam Agarwal, Director (Finance) at the state-owned explorer told analysts in a post-results call on Tuesday (August 4, 2026).
“Last year, our oil plus gas standalone production was in the range of 38.87 million metric tonnes of oil equivalent (MMTOE). This year we expect to reach about 39 MMT this year. The upside will come mainly from gas,” he stated, adding separately, “Next year, another almost 1 MMTOE of oil and gas gain will be there in FY 2027-28.”
Conducive to pursue deepwater exploration
Responding to a query, Mr. Agarwal stated that with oil prices expected to hover at about $75 per barrel, pursuing deepwater exploration would be lucrative and in turn, further the country’s energy security in the backdrop of the post West Asia conflict.
“Now, with the Hormuz crisis, there is a security layer which is coming at the baseline and we believe it [oil prices] would be $75 per barrel in the long run,” he stated.
Separately, he elaborated, “At $60-65 [per barrel prices], many of the deepwater [exploration] is high-risk, high-reward game, and the size of the reservoir is such that the economics must be very good to develop them. So, maybe some of the fields might not have good to explore at $60-65 [per barrel price regime] but at $75 [per barrel] they would be lucrative also and important for energy security.”
Mr. Agarwal also stated that the explorer is seeing positive signs for its overseas arm ONGC Videsh’s projects in Venezuela’s San Cristobal and Carabobo-1.
“Now we have full freedom to work on Venezuela project because earlier we were restricting our operations there because of the sanction-related risk. Those risks are behind us,” he stated, adding separately, “We believe very soon we will see some positive development, the new agreement signed, and we [are] taking over the operatorship for some of those projects from PDVSA.”

briefs.headline: Dalal Street outlook: Crude oil, Strait of Hormuz and Fed cues to drive stock market this week
briefs.deck: Indian stock markets are currently influenced by geopolitical tensions and global monetary conditions. Investors are particularly vigilant about developments in the Strait of Hormuz and the ongoing US-Iran conflict. Additionally, the Federal Reserve's policy decisions will likely influence investor sentiment. Fluctuations in foreign investment and crude oil prices remain significant factors…
briefs.bodyText:
After snapping a two-week winning run, Indian equities are likely to remain sensitive to geopolitical developments, with the Strait of Hormuz, US-Iran standoff and crude oil prices expected to influence trading activity this week.
According to analysts, with the quarterly earnings season now behind investors, they are focusing on global monetary policy and foreign investor flows.
"Developments surrounding the Strait of Hormuz and the trajectory of Brent crude will remain critical market drivers in the near term. With the earnings season behind us, the coming week will be relatively data-light, with investors likely to focus on global monetary policy expectations, crude oil prices and geopolitical developments," Ajit Mishra – SVP, research, Religare Broking Ltd, said.
A key event for global markets will be the release of the minutes of the US Federal Open Market Committee's July meeting. The minutes are due on August 19 and will be watched for indications on the Federal Reserve's policy outlook.
Globally, a signal of a more hawkish Fed stance could put pressure on emerging-market flows and increase volatility in Indian equities, Mishra told PTI.
"Investor attention in the coming week is likely to remain firmly focused on developments surrounding the Strait of Hormuz and the broader US–Iran standoff. 
Investor focus will also turn to the release of the minutes from the Federal Reserve's July policy meeting on August 19," Ponmudi R, CEO - Enrich Money, said.
Ponmudi also said foreign institutional flows would be another area of focus for investors.
The heightened focus on crude and geopolitical developments comes after Dalal Street ended lower last week. BSE benchmark Sensex shed 489.92 points, or 0.62%, while NSE Nifty lost 204.65 points, or 0.83%.
The decline ended a two-week winning streak for Indian equity markets, with rising crude oil prices and renewed geopolitical tensions weighing on sentiment, Ponmudi said.
Pabitro Mukherjee, deputy vice president-research, Bajaj Broking, said investors would track crude oil price movements along with developments in the ongoing US-Iran geopolitical tensions.
Besides these factors, Chinese economic data will also be watched for cues on global growth, while the FOMC minutes could offer direction on the Fed's policy outlook, Vinod Nair, head of research, Geojit Investments Limited, said.
Investors, therefore, head into a relatively data-light week with crude oil, geopolitical developments, foreign flows and signals from the US central bank among the key factors expected to guide trading activity.

briefs.headline: Bullion watch: Where are gold and silver prices headed next week? Fed minutes, Middle East in focus
briefs.deck: Gold and silver prices may continue their upward trend next week. Geopolitical and economic cues will significantly influence this momentum. Analysts expect bullion to retain its positive bias amid global data. Investors will monitor US housing, trade, and inflation figures closely. Federal Reserve meeting minutes will also provide monetary policy outlook signals.
briefs.bodyText:
Gold and silver prices could continue their upward rally next week, but the momentum will depend on geopolitical and economic cues. Analysts expect bullion to remain firm as markets weigh the latest developments in the Middle East alongside inflation, trade and other global cues.
Markets will keep an eye on US housing and trade data, inflation figures from the UK, Eurozone and Japan, and China’s economic indicators for cues on industrial metals. The minutes of the Federal Reserve’s FOMC meeting will also be closely watched for signals on the US central bank’s monetary policy outlook.
"The outlook for gold and silver remains positive and are expected to move up towards Rs 1.57 lakh per 10 grams and Rs 2.54 lakh per kg level," Pranav Mer, senior vice president, EBG - commodity & currency research, JM Financial Services Ltd, told PTI.
On the domestic front, gold futures for October delivery gained Rs 2,686, or nearly 2 per cent, last week to close at Rs 1.54 lakh per 10 grams on the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX). Silver futures for September delivery rose Rs 4,458, or 1.9 per cent, to Rs 2.35 lakh per kilogram.
"Gold traded higher this week, gaining 1 per cent, while the rally extended more than 2 per cent at the peak before profit-booking emerged at higher levels," said Jateen Trivedi, VP research analyst, commodity and currency, LKP Securities.
The sharp August run-up could, however, bring some pauses. MCX gold has gained nearly 9.5 per cent this month, making consolidation and intermittent profit-booking at higher levels more likely in the near term, Trivedi said.
Internationally, Comex gold futures for December delivery rose $37.6, or nearly 1 per cent, last week to $4,437.3 per ounce. Silver gained $1.61, or 2.5 per cent, to $65.11 an ounce in New York.
Gold futures have now closed higher for a second consecutive week, though the metal remained in consolidation after an 11 per cent rally from below $4,000 per ounce, Mer said.
Bullion prices found support after traders pared back bets on a September rate hike by the US Fed following weaker-than-expected non-farm payroll data and steady inflation. Other economic indicators remained mixed, he said.
Gold also continued to draw safe-haven demand amid the Middle East conflict and US-Iran tensions over the Strait of Hormuz, with no resolution to the conflict in sight, Mer added.
Silver, too, held on to its positive bias, although prices consolidated as the recent rally in industrial metals paused.
For bullion investors, the focus now remains firmly on three familiar forces.
According to Trivedi, the US dollar, interest-rate expectations and geopolitical developments will remain the key drivers for bullion prices.

briefs.headline: India cooks up LPG safety net: Govt fixes refinery-wise output targets; Reliance gets biggest quota
briefs.deck: India is establishing production benchmarks for its refineries and upstream firms, aimed at fortifying the domestic LPG supply system. Reliance Industries leads with the highest targets assigned to its refinery. It is imperative that companies ensure sufficient infrastructure for LPG storage and transportation. These production benchmarks will undergo reviews and updates biannually.
briefs.bodyText:
India, for the first time, has set production targets for individual public and private-sector refineries and upstream companies as it looks to build a stronger domestic supply system after the Middle East chaos disrupted imports.
In an order issued earlier this week, the petroleum and natural gas ministry set maximum LPG production levels for 21 refineries and upstream companies.
Together, they can produce up to 63,810 tonnes of LPG a day, which is more than twice India's domestic LPG production in 2025-26 and about 70% of the country's daily consumption.
The targets will apply whenever there is a shortage or disruption in supply.
Reliance gets highest target
Reliance Industries' older refinery has been given the highest target, at up to 18,000 tonnes of LPG a day.
Eighteen refineries owned and operated by public-sector oil companies have been asked to produce a total of 31,470 tonnes a day.
Reliance's 33-million-tonne-a-year domestic-tariff area (DTA) refinery at Jamnagar in Gujarat, whose products are sold in India, has been given a target of 18,000 tonnes a day. No target has been fixed for its 35.2-million-tonne-a-year refinery at the same site that is meant only for exports.
Nayara Energy's 20-million-tonne-a-year refinery at Vadinar has been given a target of 4,480 tonnes a day.
Gas producers and processors such as ONGC and GAIL, which make LPG from natural gas, have been given a combined target of 6,460 tonnes a day.
India's heavy reliance on LPG imports
India used 33.2 million tonnes of LPG in 2025-26, or about 91,000 tonnes a day.
Domestic production was 13.1 million tonnes for the year, or around 35,900 tonnes a day. Imports made up the remaining 21.3 million tonnes, or about 58,400 tonnes a day.
This meant more than 64% of India's LPG requirement came from imports.
The dependence became a problem when the Iran war effectively shut the Strait of Hormuz, the sea route through which India received 90% of its imports from countries such as Saudi Arabia.
Emergency measures raised domestic production
After imports were hit, the government in March asked refineries to divert some streams used for petrochemicals towards LPG production.
It also initially stopped sales to industrial and commercial users and later increased supplies gradually. For households, the time between LPG refill bookings was increased. Consumers were also encouraged to shift to piped natural gas, whose supplies were not as badly affected by the war.
Domestic LPG production rose to around 55,000 tonnes a day at the height of the crisis. The emergency orders asking refineries to maximise production were gradually withdrawn after supplies improved from mid-June.
The new order now sets facility-wise production levels instead of relying only on emergency directions.
Refineries told to improve LPG storage and transport
The new rules require refineries and upstream companies to maintain enough infrastructure to store, move and transport LPG. They must also take technically and economically possible steps to increase production.
The order said, "It is hereby ordered that all public sector, joint venture and private sector oil refining companies, and upstream oil companies shall develop, augment and at all times maintain adequate infrastructure for storage, evacuation and transport of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) either by itself or through other entities viz railways or road tankers adequate for the specified quantities."
Companies have also been asked to "implement all technically and economically feasible measures and technologies such as naphtha-to-LPG conversion, gasoline-based fluid catalytic cracking unit to petro-fluid catalytic cracking unit, or other upgrades, to maximise LPG production beyond current minimum producible quantities as specified in the Schedule, with intimation to Centre for High Technology or any other authorised agency, whenever such an upgrade is undertaken."
This includes converting naphtha into LPG and upgrading fluid catalytic cracking units wherever possible.
The government can direct refineries, oil marketing companies and upstream companies to increase LPG production to a specified level for a specified period if it feels this is needed to ensure enough domestic LPG and fair prices.
The ministry said "if Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary in public interest to ensure adequate availability, equitable distribution and availability at fair prices of domestic LPG, it may by itself or through Centre for High Technology or any other authorised agency, by order in writing, issue direction to oil refining companies, oil marketing companies and upstream oil companies to ramp up the LPG production levels for such quantity and period specified therein, including compliance with any restrictions on alternative uses of input streams required to produce the LPG."
Companies will have to increase production within the time set by the government.
Targets to be reviewed every six months
The government will update the production schedule on January 1 and July 1 every year.
The changes can include LPG production from new refineries and upstream companies, as well as extra production from existing facilities after changes in infrastructure, technology, evacuation, supply, transport or distribution.
The framework comes after the emergency steps taken during the Middle East crisis, when household LPG supplies were prioritised and supplies to some commercial and industrial users were restricted. The government has now put in place a system under which refineries and upstream companies can be asked to maintain or increase LPG production when supplies are disrupted.
