briefs.headline: From GST reform to GCCs: How India can become a $20 trillion economy by 2036
briefs.deck: India could reach a $20 trillion economy by 2036 with reforms. Services will drive this expansion, contributing over 65% of the GDP. A 20-step reform agenda targets taxes and capital markets for efficiency. Global capability centers and tourism offer significant growth opportunities. Successful execution of these measures is crucial for achieving the target.
briefs.bodyText:
India could become a $20 trillion economy by 2036 if it manages to raise underlying rupee growth to around 14.2% and sustain annual rupee appreciation of 3-3.6%, according to a research report by domestic brokerage Equirus.
The report has proposed a 20-step reform agenda aimed at lifting India's growth trajectory, strengthening the external balance and creating the conditions needed to achieve the ambitious dollar-denominated target.
India's economy is currently estimated at around $3.7 trillion. Reaching $20 trillion in the next decade would require the economy to expand roughly 5.5 times and sustain nominal dollar growth of about 18% a year, significantly above its historical trend of around 10-11%, the brokerage said, according to news agency ANI.
Services need to drive India's next phase of growth
Equirus said the composition of India's growth would be as important as its pace, with services expected to become the main engine of expansion.
Services currently account for about 54% of GDP and would need to contribute more than 65% as India moves towards the $20 trillion milestone. The sector's economic output would have to increase from roughly $2 trillion to more than $11 trillion, the report estimated.
Manufacturing, meanwhile, could face constraints from a more protectionist global trade environment, while agriculture's share of GDP is expected to decline as urbanisation accelerates.
India has already recorded a sharp acceleration in its economic expansion. It took the country 67 years after independence to build its first $2 trillion economy, while the economy nearly doubled during the decade after 2014.
20 reforms target taxes, capital markets and human capital
The proposed reform package spans the real economy, capital markets, human capital, services and urban governance.
Among the measures suggested by Equirus are bringing fuel under the GST regime, setting minimum capital-expenditure floors for states, listing the Railways, creating an Indian sovereign fund, expanding private education capacity and reviving private-sector research and development.
The report also calls for deeper corporate bond markets and measures to reduce tax-related working-capital pressures.
It estimates that abolishing advance tax could release around Rs 10 trillion of working capital, while moving to a flat 5% TDS could unlock another Rs 13.4 trillion.
The reforms are intended not only to increase economic activity but also to improve the efficiency with which capital is deployed across the economy.
GCCs, tourism seen as major growth opportunities
The report puts particular emphasis on India's services economy, including global capability centres (GCCs).
A proposed National GCC policy could increase the number of GCCs in India from more than 1,800 to 5,000, potentially generating an economic impact of $470-600 billion and creating 20-25 million jobs, Equirus estimated.
Tourism is another area identified as having significant potential. Greater promotion of the sector could potentially add around $21 billion a year in foreign exchange receipts, the brokerage said.
Overall, Equirus estimates that its reform package could generate about Rs 7.9 trillion in annual direct gains, against costs of roughly Rs 3.4 trillion. This would result in an estimated net annual gain of Rs 4.5 trillion.
The report cautioned that reaching $20 trillion would ultimately depend on execution across several areas rather than any single policy measure.
Sustaining rapid growth while improving the rupee's external value and expanding high-productivity services would be central to India's ability to meet the 2036 target.

briefs.headline: Government sets LPG production targets for refiners; Reliance gets largest quota
briefs.deck: The Petroleum and Natural Gas Ministry has specified maximum LPG production levels for 21 refineries and upstream companies, with combined production potential set at 63,810 tonnes a day
briefs.bodyText:
The government has for the first time fixed maximum cooking gas LPG production targets for individual public- and private-sector refineries and upstream companies, as it seeks to build a domestic supply buffer after the West Asia conflict exposed the country's vulnerability to disruptions in imported cooking gas.
The Petroleum and Natural Gas Ministry, in an order issued on August 13, has specified maximum LPG production levels for 21 refineries and upstream companies, with combined production potential set at 63,810 tonnes a day -- more than double the domestic LPG output in the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 and about 70% of the country's daily consumption.
The production limits will kick in whenever there is a supply constraint.
The lion's share of the planned output has been set from Reliance Industries Ltd's older refinery, which would have to produce up to 18,000 tonnes a day of LPG, according to the order.
India consumed 33.2 million tonnes of LPG in the 2025-26 fiscal year (about 91,000 tonnes per day). Of this, 13.1 million tonnes a year was produced locally (about 35,900 tonnes per day), while the remaining 21.3 million tonnes per annum (about 58,400 tonnes a day) was imported.
This high import dependence of over 64% left the country exposed when the start of the Iran war effectively shut the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow sea lane through which India got 90% of its imports from nations like Saudi Arabia.
With supplies impacted, the government in March ordered refineries to divert streams used for petrochemical production to maximise LPG output.
It also initially stopped sales to industrial and commercial users and thereafter gradually scaled it up. For domestic households, the frequency of booking a refill was increased, and they were encouraged to shift to piped natural gas, whose supplies were not so severely impacted due to the war.
Domestic production was ramped up to about 55,000 tonnes a day at the height of the crisis. Still, the emergency orders asking refiners to maximise output were gradually withdrawn after supplies eased from mid-June.
The new order goes further than the emergency one issued during the West Asia crisis by establishing facility-specific production benchmarks and requiring refiners and upstream companies to maintain adequate infrastructure for LPG storage, evacuation, and transportation. Companies must also pursue technically and economically feasible upgrades to maximise output.
The government has empowered itself to order refiners, oil marketing companies and upstream producers to ramp up LPG production for specified quantities and periods whenever it considers such action necessary to ensure adequate domestic availability, equitable distribution and supply at fair prices.
The production schedule will be reviewed every six months, allowing the government to add output from new refineries and upstream fields and account for additional capacity created through technology and infrastructure upgrades.
The order also requires refiners to consider measures such as converting naphtha into LPG and upgrading fluid catalytic cracking units where technically and economically viable, underscoring the government's push to extract more LPG from existing refining infrastructure.
The government had introduced several emergency measures during the West Asia crisis, including prioritising household LPG supplies and restricting supplies to some commercial and industrial users as imports were disrupted.
The new production framework is aimed at ensuring that a future disruption to overseas LPG supplies does not translate into the shortages and rationing seen during the recent crisis.
Taking lessons from the crisis, the government has now put the country's refineries and upstream producers under a standing framework to maintain and, when necessary, increase LPG output.
Eighteen refineries owned and operated by public sector oil companies have been ordered to produce a total of 31,470 tonnes a day.
In the private sector, Reliance's 33 million tonnes-a-year domestic tariff area (DTA) refinery at Jamnagar in Gujarat, products from which are sold locally, has been ordered to produce 18,000 tonnes. No target has been set for Reliance's 35.2 million tonnes a year only-for-exports refinery at the same site.
Russia's Rosneft-backed Nayara Energy's 20 million tonnes-a-year Vadinar refinery has been asked to produce 4,480 tonnes a day, according to the order.
Upstream gas producers and processors like ONGC and GAIL, which make LPG from natural gas, have been given a target of 6,460 tonnes a day.
"It is hereby ordered that all public sector, joint venture and private sector oil refining companies, and upstream oil companies shall develop, augment and at all times maintain adequate infrastructure for storage, evacuation and transport of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) either by itself or through other entities, viz railways or road tankers adequate for the specified quantities," the order said.
They were also ordered to "implement all technically and economically feasible measures and technologies such as naphtha-to-LPG conversion, gasoline-based fluid catalytic cracking unit to petro-fluid catalytic cracking unit, or other upgrades, to maximise LPG production beyond current minimum producible quantities as specified in the Schedule, with intimation to Centre for High Technology or any other authorised agency, whenever such an upgrade is undertaken." The ministry further said "if central government is of the opinion that it is necessary in public interest to ensure adequate availability, equitable distribution and availability at fair prices of domestic LPG, it may by itself or through Centre for High Technology or any other authorised agency, by order in writing, issue direction to oil refining companies, oil marketing companies and upstream oil companies to ramp up the LPG production levels for such quantity and period specified therein, including compliance with any restrictions on alternative uses of input streams required to produce the LPG." Whenever directions are issued, the companies will have to ramp-up LPG production levels within the stipulated time frame.
The central government, the order said, shall update the production schedule on January 1 and July 1 of every year, including updates to LPG production from new refineries and upstream oil companies or additional LPG quantities from existing refineries and upstream companies due to changes to associated infrastructure and production technology, evacuation, supply, transport or distribution of LPG.

briefs.headline: Even as government considers MDR charge on UPI, data shows cash usage quickening in economy
briefs.deck: An analysis by The Hindu shows that the growth in the value of UPI transactions has been consistently slowing since 2021-22, although the current rate of growth is still higher than that of cash with the public
briefs.bodyText:
At a time when the government is proposing to allow the levy of a charge on UPI transactions, an analysis shows that the growth in the value of UPI transactions has been slowing for the last five years, while the growth of cash with the public has been quickening over this period.
Paywall: On a charge on UPI transactions
While slowing, the growth of UPI transactions remains faster than the growth of cash among the public, but this margin is shrinking. Experts say this is both a sign of higher economic activity and higher price levels than are being reflected in the official inflation data.
UPI and RuPay debit card transactions are currently free, like cash transactions. However, the government passed the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 in the recently-concluded Monsoon session of Parliament, which enables it to allow a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) charge to be levied on these electronic transactions.
Cash is back
An analysis by The Hindu of data from the Reserve Bank of India shows that the growth rate of cash with the public reached a recent high of about 17% in the COVID-19 pandemic year of 2020-21. Thereafter, the growth of cash with the public fell consistently until 2023-24, where it hit about 4%.
Cash with the public is the total cash in circulation minus what is sitting in banks.
Since then, the growth of cash with the public has been quickening. That is, this growth rate rose to 6.5% in 2024-25 and further to 12% in 2025-26. In 2026-27, cash with the public, at ₹41.8 lakh crore as of July 31, 2026, was nearly 13% higher than in the same period of the previous year.
Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and the Payments Corporation of India have made assurances that the general public would not have to pay the MDR charge on UPI transactions and that it would only be levied on certain high value merchants and transactions.
However, the Opposition has said that the merchants who do have to pay this charge would pass that higher cost onto their customers in the form of higher prices and that this could push people back to using cash.
UPI slowing but high
UPI transactions, on the other hand, have seen their growth slowing over the last few years, as per data with the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). The value of UPI transactions conducted in the country grew 133% in 2019-20, which then slowed to a relatively robust 95% in 2020-21 as the economy locked down.
It then quickened again to 105% in 2021-22 as the economy opened up and pent-up demand combined with health fears over handling cash to push up UPI usage.
Since then, however, the growth in the value of transactions done on the UPI platform has consistently been slowing, with growth hitting 20.3% in 2025-26. In 2026-27, this has further slowed to 18.7% as of August 2026, as compared to the April-August period of last year.
However, this 18.7% growth in UPI transactions is still higher than the 13% growth in cash with the public in the same period.
Inflation likely understated
According to Pronab Sen, former Chief Statistician of India and former Chairman of the Standing Committee on Statistics, the fact that both cash and UPI are growing should be showing itself in the form of higher inflation rates than what the official numbers are currently showing.
“This would imply that we are undercounting inflation, because that’s where this should show up,” Mr. Sen told The Hindu. “If there is more money being transacted, both digitally and in cash, then that should show up in inflation. The first effect would be there.”
“A lot of this could be explained if the official data showed prices were rising faster than they are,” he added.
The latest official retail inflation data for July 2026 stood at 4.45%, slightly higher than in June, while the wholesale data showed inflation had slowed marginally to 9.8% in July from 9.9% in June.
Signs of robust economy
D.K. Srivastava, chief policy advisor at EY India, says that simultaneous cash and UPI growth is a sign of a vibrant economy.
“The first reason is increasing economic activity in general,” Mr. Srivastava said. “That is to say, high growth rates. We have been maintaining a real growth rate in excess of 7% in the post-COVID years. That is the main reason why both cash transactions and digital transactions have increased.”
Mr. Sen, however, warned that an increase in cash transactions could also point towards distress in the economy brought on by high unemployment, especially among the youth.

stories.headline: Cancelo joins Barca permanently after Al Hilal exit, set to sign on Tuesday
stories.deck: João Cancelo is set to return to Barcelona for a third spell after terminating his Al Hilal contract by mutual agreement. The Portugal international will join the Spanish champions as a free agent after two previous loan spells, having helped Barcelona win LaLiga last season. Cancelo is expected in Barcelona on Tuesday to complete his move and sign a permanent contract.
stories.bodyText:
João Cancelo is set to return to Barcelona for a third spell after reaching an agreement to terminate his contract with Al Hilal, clearing the way for the Portugal international to rejoin the Spanish champions as a free agent.
The 32-year-old had one year remaining on his contract in Saudi Arabia, but his desire to return to Barcelona has now been matched by an agreement that allows him to leave without a transfer fee. He is expected in Barcelona on Tuesday to complete the move and sign his contract.
Cancelo finally gets the permanent Barcelona move
Cancelo had already agreed personal terms with Barcelona in June, with the remaining obstacle being his situation at Al Hilal. That has now been resolved after the player and Saudi club reached an agreement on an early termination.
According to sources cited by ESPN, Cancelo will join Barcelona as a free agent after previously spending two loan spells at the club. He first arrived from Manchester City for the 2023-24 season before returning to Al Hilal, then came back to Barcelona on loan during the second half of last season.
That second spell proved important. Cancelo helped Barcelona win LaLiga and made it clear that he wanted to remain at the club permanently.
The situation had appeared difficult because Al Hilal had initially valued him at around €10 million, before reportedly raising their asking price to €15 million. Barcelona's preference was to avoid a significant transfer fee, and the eventual termination of Cancelo's Saudi contract has removed that obstacle.
He is now set to make the move without Barcelona having to negotiate a transfer fee with Al Hilal.
A third arrival, but a first permanent signing
This will technically be Cancelo's third time signing for Barcelona, although it will be the first occasion on which he joins on a permanent contract.
His first spell began in August 2023, when Barcelona signed him on loan from Manchester City for the 2023-24 campaign. Financial limitations meant they could not turn that arrangement into a permanent transfer, and Cancelo subsequently moved from City to Al Hilal.
He returned to Barcelona in January 2026 on another six-month loan from the Saudi club and helped the team secure the LaLiga title.
The Portugal international has now secured the permanent return he had been seeking.
Before reaching the top level with Manchester City and Barcelona, Cancelo came through at Benfica and also played for Valencia, Inter Milan and Juventus. He spent part of 2023 on loan at Bayern Munich before joining Al Hilal in 2024.
His honours include league titles in Portugal, England, Italy, Germany and Spain, making him the first player this century to win the top-flight title in four of Europe's five major leagues.
Barcelona's summer plans gather pace
Cancelo becomes Barcelona's fourth signing of the summer, following Anthony Gordon, Karim Adeyemi and Jesse Bisiwu.
The club's recruitment has continued to develop rapidly, with 
Rodri also reportedly agreeing a €76.5 million ($88.4 million)
 move from Manchester City on the same day. That would reunite Cancelo with his former City team-mate in a Barcelona squad that has already retained the Spanish league title and is looking to strengthen further.
Barcelona are also pursuing a striker, with Atlético Madrid's Julián Álvarez reported to be their preferred target, while another No. 9 and potentially a centre-back remain under consideration.
After Sunday's 5-2 friendly victory over Basel, manager Hansi Flick acknowledged that more business could still take place.
“We will see what happens, but it could be that we are still lacking something,” Flick said.
For Cancelo, however, the uncertainty is largely over. After two temporary stays in Catalonia and an increasingly complicated spell in Saudi Arabia, he is now expected to return to Barcelona on Tuesday with the opportunity to finally make the Camp Nou his permanent home.

stories.headline: Barcelona finally get Rodri after third offer as Man City accept €76.5m deal
stories.deck: Barcelona have reportedly agreed a €76.5 million deal to sign Rodri from Manchester City. The Spain captain is set to return to La Liga after seven trophy-filled seasons in England. Rodri, who won the 2026 World Cup and Golden Ball, could be presented before Barcelona’s Joan Gamper Trophy match, while City prepare to lose their midfield anchor.
stories.bodyText:
Barcelona have reportedly reached an agreement in principle to sign Rodri from Manchester City, with the Spain captain set to return to La Liga after seven trophy-filled seasons in England.
The proposed deal is understood to be worth €76.5 million (about $88.4 million) in total, after Barcelona returned with a third offer for the 30-year-old midfielder. Rodri is set to sign a four-year contract with the La Liga champions. The move would bring one of the world's most accomplished midfielders back to Spain just weeks after he captained the country to the 2026 World Cup and was named the tournament's best player.
Barcelona return with third offer
Barcelona had already seen two approaches for Rodri rejected before returning with an improved proposal over the weekend.
According to sources cited by ESPN and 
The Athletic
, Barcelona’s third offer takes the total package to €76.5 million ($88.4m). City will receive an upfront €60 million ($68.8m), with more than €11 million in highly achievable bonuses, and the Premier League club expects to receive at least €71.5 million overall for Rodri, who has less than 12 months left on his contract.
Rodri is expected to travel to Barcelona in the coming days and could be presented before Wednesday's Joan Gamper Trophy match against Al Ahly at Spotify Camp Nou.
The agreement follows a summer in which Rodri's future had become increasingly uncertain. He was entering the final year of his Manchester City contract, giving the English club a reason to consider a sale if the right offer arrived.
Barcelona's interest also developed after Frenkie de Jong suffered a long-term injury, prompting the Spanish champions to explore the midfield market more seriously.
Rodri was not initially considered a priority target, but his availability changed the picture. Barcelona then moved ahead with their pursuit, while sources told ESPN that the midfielder preferred a return to Spain with Barça over a move to Real Madrid.
A statement signing for Barcelona
Barcelona see Rodri as a major addition to a squad that has won consecutive Spanish league titles and are understood to view him as a player capable of strengthening Hansi Flick's side for the coming seasons.
His arrival would also add another established leader to a summer recruitment drive that has already brought Anthony Gordon, Karim Adeyemi and Jesse Bisiwu to the club.
João Cancelo is also set to return to Barcelona as a free agent, according to sources cited by ESPN, while the club continue to pursue a striker. Atlético Madrid's Julián Álvarez is their leading target following the departures of 
Robert Lewandowski
 and Ferran Torres.
Rodri's experience would be particularly valuable in a squad preparing to compete on multiple fronts. He has won at the highest level in both club and international football, while his ability to control games from midfield has made him one of the defining players in his position.
Rodri leaves City after seven seasons
Rodri joined Manchester City from Atlético Madrid in 2019 after previously playing for Villarreal and Atlético.
Across 298 appearances in seven seasons, he helped City win 12 major honours, including four Premier League titles, two FA Cups, three EFL Cups and the Champions League in 2022-23.
His time in England was interrupted by a serious knee injury that ruled him out for much of the 2024-25 campaign, while a hamstring problem also disrupted parts of last season.
He returned to his best level at the 2026 World Cup, captaining Spain to the title after a 1-0 extra-time victory over Argentina. Rodri was also awarded the Golden Ball as the tournament's best player.
The World Cup triumph followed his success at Euro 2024, where he was also named player of the tournament. That performance helped him win the 2024 Ballon d'Or.
Rodri with the 2024 Ballon d'Or trophy
Rodri would therefore leave Manchester City having added almost every major honour available to his collection.
City prepare for life without their midfield anchor
Barcelona's opening proposal was reportedly rejected last week, with City turning down an offer worth around €45.2 million ($52.2 million) before the Catalan club increased its bid.
After Sunday's Community Shield defeat by Arsenal, new City manager Enzo Maresca acknowledged the difficulty of replacing a player of Rodri's calibre.
“Rodri is a player who just won the World Cup and Ballon d'Or,” Maresca said. “He's a top player, all the teams need a Rodri, so it's not about if we miss Rodri or not.”
Manchester City's Rodri . (AP Photo)
Rodri's departure would bring an end to his seven-year spell at the Etihad and leave City without a midfielder who has been central to their most successful period.
For Barcelona, meanwhile, the agreement would bring home a player who has already won a World Cup, European Championship and Ballon d'Or, while still being 30 years old and entering what could be several important seasons at the Camp Nou.

stories.headline: Cristiano Ronaldo hints at retirement, says upcoming year could be his last
stories.deck: Ronaldo, whose Al Nassr contract runs until June 2027, previously has stopped short of ‌giving a timeline of when he’d be ready to call ‌it a career
stories.bodyText:
Cristiano Ronaldo is inching closer to retirement.
“This is probably my last year of football, and I want to leave a spectacular legacy,” Ronaldo, 41, told Vogue in an interview published on Sunday (August 16, 2026).
Ronaldo, whose Al Nassr contract runs until June 2027, previously has stopped short of giving a timeline of when he’d be ready to call it a career.
Ronaldo announced his retirement from World Cup play but did not close the door on making future appearances for the national team. He is Portugal’s all-time leader in caps (233) and goals (146) and in 2026 joined Argentina’s Lionel Messi as the only man to appear in six World Cups.
Ronaldo scored three goals in the 2026 World Cup but was the subject of criticism from disappointed fans.
“I have my future all mapped out,” Ronaldo told Vogue. “I have so many things to keep me busy that to tell you just one thing is hard.
“Because football could leave a big hole, you have to fill your time in various ways, not just one. And also have more fun, travel more, watch and play padel, which I really like, and continue to enjoy what I’ve earned — what we’ve earned. Because after all it’s been 25 years with a lot of sacrifice,” he added.
A five-time Ballon d’Or winner, Ronaldo started his career at Sporting CP before competing with Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus.

stories.headline: Not going to overthink, says skipper Harmanpreet Singh about over-reliance on PCs
stories.bodyText:
Harmanpreet Singh scores, India wins. But what happens when he doesn’t?
Harmanpreet had a wry smile when a question on similar lines was put forward to him. It’s a query he has faced countless times in his long career and one he was probably half-expecting after India’s 3-1 World Cup victory over Wales here on Saturday.
The Indian skipper once again showed why he is among the world’s greatest when it comes to dragflicks, scoring twice and taking his goal tally to 254. All three of India’s goals came from short corners, with Sanjay Rana also netting one from the area.
Is there an over-reliance on penalty corners? What about the field goals?
Harmanpreet was quick to defend his forwards although the link-up between Mandeep Singh, Abhishek Nain and Sukhjeet Singh lacked the final pass, control or finishing touch in the clash against Wales.
“They are playing well. They are creating so many chances in the D, so it doesn’t matter if we are scoring a field goal or creating a PC. At the end of the day, we are getting goals, that’s more important,” said the 30-year-old.
In recent years, India has relied on its prowess from short corners, particularly from the stick of Harmanpreet. After all, of his 254 goals, a whopping 217 (85.43%) have come from PCs. India wins 69% of the matches when Harmanpreet scores.
When his penalty-corner conversion form dipped in his stop-start Pro League campaign, India struggled woefully in front of goal to finish eighth in the standings. In the 10 games he featured, the team converted just nine of its 43 PCs with Harmanpreet managing a lowly two. The overall picture across 16 games highlighted India’s poor PC conversion and its struggles from open play, which led to a sub-par number of short corners earned.
Of its 63 PCs, 24 came in the two matches against last-placed Pakistan. In 14 games against the top-seven teams, several of whom will be strong contenders at the World Cup, India converted just eight of the 39 short corners.
While India scored more field goals (16) than PC goals (13) in the Pro League, it should be noted that six of them came against Pakistan. Harmanpreet doesn’t want to look back on India’s struggles and maintains that the objective is clear. “We are not going to overthink things. We know our values and targets. We are here for the World Cup, we are going to win this,” he said.

briefs.headline: Ever-hungry Sindhu targets record sixth Worlds medal
briefs.bodyText:
Five-time World championships medallist P.V. Sindhu will look for a record-breaking sixth prize as she begins her campaign here on Monday. A half dozen medals will make her the first women’s singles player to achieve the feat in the tournament.
Fresh from ending a long wait for a title at the Japan Open, Sindhu said the triumph had given her the confidence for the World championships. “It has been quite good, physically and mentally. I have been able to see the changes in terms of my game and my movement,” she said.
One thing that has remained throughout her career, she said, is her “hunger towards the game”.
“I know it is in me and I can still do it.”
But the game has evolved, with women’s singles becoming more demanding. “Women’s singles used to be more attacking and fast-paced. Now it is more about long rallies, patience and staying on court for a longer period,” she said.
Experience, she added, has helped her deal with conditions that can force players to alter their style.
“I’m much more experienced now in terms of how to deal with different conditions on court.
“Sometimes there is drift, and sometimes you cannot control the shuttle the way you want.
“You have to change accordingly and make things convenient for yourself.”
The home setting brings added expectations, but the pressure that comes with playing a high-stakes match is nothing new to her.
“I have played a lot of first-round matches where I had butterflies and there is a lot of pressure… at the same time, there is nothing to lose. I just want to give my best because I have trained hard and I have worked hard in my training session”.

briefs.headline: Badminton Worlds: Indian hopes rest on Sindhu, Satwik-Chirag pair
briefs.deck: Ayush takes on defending champion Shi in the opening round; Lakshya attempts to script history
briefs.bodyText:
The badminton World championships starting here on Monday will be as much a test of India’s growth in the sport as a show of its organisational abilities both on and off the court.
The last time India hosted the marquee event in 2009, it had a grand total of one medal in the tournament’s history. Since then, the country has not gone without one in the 11 editions starting 2011.
P.V. Sindhu, with five medals including the lone Indian gold under her belt, carries the hopes yet again. The ninth seed will begin her campaign against world No. 141 Sofia Nobel of Ireland. The road to the top will be anything but easy for the 31-year-old in her 10th Worlds. China’s Wang Zhi Yi, Putri Kusuma Wardani of Indonesia and top-ranked An Se Young of Korea could come in her way. The 2019 gold was also her last medal in the mega event. However, Sindhu has found form in recent times, clinching the Japan Open Super 750 crown last month.
“I think winning the Japan Open gave me a lot of of confidence. Having five medals is an amazing journey...each gave me a different kind of experience. I think the transition has been wonderful. When I lost the 2017 World championships (to Japan’s Nozomi Okuhara in the final), I was very hard on myself... And there were times where I’ve lost where I was leading. These are some of the moments that made me stronger,” Sindhu admitted on the eve of the competition.
Defending champion Akane Yamaguchi of Japan will be looking to become the first women’s singles player to win four golds, going past Spain’s Carolina Marin.
Also hoping to put their recent injury woes behind and add to their collection would be Asian Games gold medallists Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty. The top Indian men’s doubles pair has got a bye in the opening round.
On Monday, Indian youngster Ayush Shetty takes on defending champion and top seed Shi Yuqi in the opening round. The 21-year-old is eyeing a first win in four meetings against the Chinese. “I think it is tough in whichever round you are playing Shi. I hope it will be great match,” said Ayush, who is making his debut in the showpiece.
Lakshya Sen, attempting to become the first Indian man to win two medals, will begin against Collins Filimon of Austria on Tuesday. He is likely to run into former champion Thai Kunlavut Vitidsarn in the pre-quarterfinals.
India’s Ashith Surya and Amrutha Pramuthesh have been promoted to the mixed doubles main draw.

Doubles: M.R. Arjun & Hariharan Amsakarunan vs. Scott Guildea & Paul Reynolds (Ire).
Women: Singles: P.V. Sindhu vs. Sofia Nobel (Ire).
Doubles: Treesa Jolly & Gayatri Gopichand vs. Paula Lopez & Lucia Rodriguez (ESP); Kavipriya Selvam & Simran Singhi vs. Nikol Carulla & Carmen Maria Jimenez (Esp).

briefs.headline: Durand Cup: SC Delhi turns the tables on Raengdai, meets East Bengal
briefs.bodyText:
Former champion East Bengal FC edged past Indian Army FT 1-0 in the second quarterfinal of the 135th Durand Cup at the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata on Sunday.
The Kolkata outfit will face Sporting Club Delhi in the semifinal at the same venue on Wednesday. The latter had defeated FC Raengdai 5-1 in the first last-eight clash.
Vishnu strikes
P.V. Vishnu scored in the 39th minute, heading home a well-delivered cross from Christopher Ikonomidis to give East Bengal the lead.
The host dominated the first half and created several chances, but Army goalkeeper Bhabindra Malla Thakuri made a series of impressive saves.
East Bengal, which recently qualified for AFC Champions League Two, struggled to convert its opportunities after the break. However, its defence held firm.
At the Birsa Munda Stadium in Ranchi, SC Delhi produced a remarkable second-half comeback and netted five goals to turn the tables on debutant Raengdai.
Chongtham Kishan Singh gave the Noney-based Manipur side the lead with a spectacular long-range strike in the ninth minute.
Inspired change
After half-time, SC Delhi coach Tomasz Tchorz introduced India under-23 forward Joseph Sunny.
The move paid off as Sunny scored twice within 10 minutes to put Delhi 2-1 ahead by the 67th minute.
Rodriguinho, Juan Sebastian Pena and Augustine Lalrochana added a goal each as Delhi roared back in style.

At Kolkata: East Bengal FC 1 (P.V. Vishnu 39) bt Indian Army FT 0.

briefs.headline: Arsenal crush Man City 3-0 in Community Shield, hand Maresca nightmare start
briefs.deck: Arsenal thrashed Manchester City 3-0 in the Community Shield, scoring within 24 seconds through Riccardo Calafiori. Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard added further goals as City struggled. Erling Haaland had just seven touches before being substituted, while Rodri’s absence exposed midfield concerns. Arsenal captain Odegaard said the team is ready to challenge for trophies again.
briefs.bodyText:
Arsenal made a strong statement ahead of the new Premier League season, beating Manchester City 3-0 in the Community Shield on Sunday. It was a difficult first competitive match for City manager Enzo Maresca, with Arsenal scoring within 24 seconds.
Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring after just 23 seconds, before Kai Havertz doubled Arsenal’s lead in the 28th minute. Martin Odegaard then added a third shortly after halftime, leaving City struggling to create meaningful chances.
Arsenal captain Odegaard was delighted with the performance as his team prepares to begin its title defence.
“I think we showed our level today — that we are ready,” Odegaard said. “We are serious and we want to do it again.”
Arsenal Punish City’s Mistakes
Calafiori finished from Myles Lewis-Skelly’s clever through ball to give Arsenal their fastest Community Shield goal in more than five decades.
Havertz then took advantage of a mistake from City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, heading the ball past him to make it 2-0. Odegaard added the third early in the second half after finding plenty of space inside the City box and sending Donnarumma the wrong way with a clever dummy.
Arsenal fans even aimed chants of “You're getting sacked in the morning” at Maresca during a match in which City rarely tested goalkeeper David Raya.
Erling Haaland, who had only recently returned to training, had just seven touches before being replaced in the 53rd minute.
City Face Early Questions
City were also without Rodri, who is recovering from minor back surgery amid reports linking him with a possible move to Barcelona. His absence leaves a major gap in midfield, with new signing Elliot Anderson expected to help fill the void.
Maresca’s decision to introduce Jack Grealish at halftime also attracted attention. Grealish spent last season on loan at Everton, and his appearance could be a sign that he still has a role to play at City.
Arsenal begin their Premier League campaign against Coventry on Friday, while City host Bournemouth two days later.

briefs.headline: Arsenal’s Calafiori scripts history with fastest-ever Community Shield goal in 118 years
briefs.deck: Riccardo Calafiori scored after just 23 seconds against Manchester City to give Arsenal a record-breaking start in the 2026 Community Shield. His strike became the fastest goal in the competition’s 118-year history, beating Liverpool legend Gary McAllister’s previous Cardiff record. Arsenal then doubled their advantage through Kai Havertz, giving Mikel Arteta’s side an impressive opening to the…
briefs.bodyText:
Riccardo Calafiori needed only 23 seconds to put Arsenal ahead against Manchester City in the 2026 FA Community Shield, producing an extraordinary opening to the traditional curtain-raiser for the English football season. The Italian defender's finish in Cardiff did more than give Mikel Arteta's side an immediate advantage: it established the quickest goal ever recorded in the 118-year history of the competition.
Calafiori makes Community Shield history
Arsenal had barely begun their first attack when Calafiori found himself running into the Manchester City penalty area. Myles Lewis-Skelly produced the decisive moment of invention, playing a precise reverse pass into the Italian's path just seconds after kick-off.
Calafiori held off his marker and calmly guided his finish past Gianluigi Donnarumma, finding the bottom-left corner to make it 1-0 after only 23 seconds.
The goal was subsequently recognised as the fastest in Community Shield history. It was also the first goal scored inside the opening minute of the competition since Manchester City's Bobby Owen did so in 1968.
For Calafiori, it was an especially notable way to begin Arsenal's campaign after joining a side that had earned its place in the Shield by finally ending its 22-year wait for the Premier League title in 2025-26.
A record that stretches back 118 years
The Community Shield has been the traditional meeting point between the champions of England and the previous season's FA Cup winners since the competition began as the FA Charity Shield in 1908. It was renamed the FA Community Shield in 2002, but its place in the football calendar has remained largely unchanged: one match, played before the league season begins, with no Premier League points or standings at stake.
That history made the speed of Calafiori's goal all the more remarkable. The previous benchmark for a particularly fast start at the Cardiff venue came in 2001, when Liverpool's Gary McAllister converted a penalty after 75 seconds against Manchester United, following Roy Keane's foul on Danny Murphy. Liverpool eventually won that match 2-1.
Calafiori had beaten that mark before the game had even reached the half-minute mark. His 23-second finish was 52 seconds quicker than McAllister's, giving Arsenal an early piece of Community Shield history before the contest had properly settled.
Arsenal's record and City's status as holders
Arsenal entered the 2026 match chasing their 18th Community Shield triumph, having previously lifted the trophy 17 times. Their most recent success came in 2023, when they faced Manchester City at Wembley.
That meeting ended 1-1 after normal time before Arsenal prevailed 4-1 on penalties.
Manchester City, meanwhile, had won the Shield seven times, with their most recent triumph coming in 2024. They therefore entered the Cardiff fixture as the holders.
Manchester United remain the most successful club in the competition's history, with 21 victories.
The 2026 edition also marked the Community Shield's return to Cardiff for the first time in 20 years. The Principality Stadium hosted the fixture annually from 2001 to 2006 while Wembley was being rebuilt.
Arsenal's new-look side makes immediate impact
The fixture brought together last season's Premier League champions and FA Cup winners, with Arsenal qualifying after their title triumph and Manchester City earning their place by beating Chelsea in the FA Cup final.
Arteta handed starts to summer arrivals Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis, while Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice and Martin Zubimendi began among the substitutes.
At centre-back, Cristhian Mosquera partnered Gabriel with William Saliba injured, while Calafiori started at left-back.
City were beginning a new era under Enzo Maresca, who had succeeded Pep Guardiola. Elliot Anderson made his start in midfield, with Phil Foden, Jeremy Doku and Antoine Semenyo supporting Erling Haaland, while Donnarumma started in goal.
Arsenal's early advantage was not an isolated moment. Tzolis later provided his first assist for the club when he nodded the ball back across goal for Kai Havertz, who headed in Arsenal's second before the half-hour mark.
That made Calafiori's 23-second strike more than simply a record-breaking opening goal. It set the tone for an Arsenal side beginning a new season with a new-look squad, against a Manchester City team entering its own period of transition.

briefs.headline: 'Very important draw': Head coach Marijne after India hold China to 2-2 stalemate
briefs.deck: India held world No. 4 China to a 2-2 draw in their Hockey World Cup opener, a positive result with 11 debutants. Coach Sjoerd Marijne praised their resilience, while Navneet Kaur impressed in attack. The draw eased pressure ahead of the next match against South Africa, though Marijne stressed the need to improve ball retention and maintain intensity.
briefs.bodyText:
India’s 2-2 draw against world No. 4 China in their Hockey World Cup opener was a major positive, especially with 11 players making their tournament debuts, head coach Sjoerd Marijne said on Sunday.
India took the lead twice, but China, the 2024 Olympic silver medallists, fought back to earn a point. Marijne was pleased with the performance but felt India could have won if they had earned a late penalty corner.
“With 11 debutants in the team, a draw against the world No. number four is very good for the future,” Marijne said after the match.
India Show Resilience Against China
India had already used their video referral when they appealed for a penalty corner late in the game, leaving them unable to review the decision.
“We had a clear PC but the referee was at an angle where she couldn't see it and you really can't blame her. We really need to learn about the video referrals,” Marijne said.
India struggled in the third quarter but responded strongly in the final period.
“The third quarter was not that good but then we came back. The resilience of the team was good and I am happy with that. We did much better in the last quarter,” he said.
The draw also eased the pressure ahead of India’s remaining Pool D matches.
“It is a very important draw. If we had lost this one, the next two would have been must-win matches. Now we don't have to do much calculations about who is winning against whom and we can focus on our own game,” he said.
Navneet Shines as India Look Ahead
Marijne praised Navneet Kaur, saying her performances showed India have attacking options beyond star drag-flicker Deepika.
“Everyone was talking about Deepika during the Nations Cup but Navneet scored equally well and in the World Cup qualifiers too. So it's not only about Deepika,” Marijne said.
Navneet said India had ignored China’s reputation and focused on their own game.
“It was a tough match but we did exceptionally well. We were leading twice and we have to do better in maintaining the lead,” she said.
India next face South Africa, with captain Salima Tete stressing that the team must maintain its intensity.
“We are happy with the one point but we will have to fight in every match and we are geared up for that,” Salima said.

briefs.headline: IND vs SL Test Day 2 | I go there and do what the team needs, says Jurel
briefs.deck: The wicketkeeper-batter chips in with a vital fifty in India’s first innings in the opening Test against Sri Lanka
briefs.bodyText:
Progress in a Test is not just about the big knock or the five-for spell, equally it is about efficient performances that slip into the shadows. Dhruv Jurel’s 51 was a vital contribution during India’s first innings in the opening Test against Sri Lanka, and the wicketkeeper-batter said: “Whenever I go in, I just think about what the team needs.”
Speaking to the media at the Galle International Stadium on Sunday (August 16, 2026), Jurel added: “There is no personal milestone that I look for before batting. I listen to the captain and coach. I go there and do what the team needs, I try to control the situation for the team. It is about being switched on. I had played in the A-series earlier here and I had an idea about the pitch and the weather.”
Asked if he felt any pressure over his spot in the playing XI, ahead of this game, Jurel countered: “Not at all. I am very grateful that I have the opportunity to represent India. That’s the only privilege that I play for.”
And as for the urgency on display from the Indian batters, Jurel said: “The plan was to make as many runs as possible by playing sensible cricket. Be it Rishabh Pant or me or the tail, we wanted runs on the board.”
Having wrested the initial honours during the first innings, Jurel felt that now it is the turn of the Indian bowlers to drive home the advantage.“Satisfaction is about winning the match. Our bowlers have to be consistent, bowl long spells. There is no rocket science. We need to put the ball in right areas and get those 20 wickets. Our score of 450-odd is very good on this pitch.”
Jurel also pointed out the value of the extended time that India had in Sri Lanka ahead of the Tests. “For India, it is all about volume. We came here 10 days before and trained at Colombo. We had many sessions. Batting on these surfaces helps us improve, and we become aware about the environment and the situation.”
The remainder of this rain-affected Test would be interesting and Jurel said: “The three days will be crucial. We have to work hard on all these days. We cannot be thinking about the time we lost to the rains”.

briefs.headline: ‘Unwanted record’: Ex-captain stunned after bizarre blunder by Pak at World Cup
briefs.deck: Pakistan's hockey captain received a green card after gear was forgotten. This incident occurred during their opening World Cup match against England. The team failed to produce necessary protective equipment for a penalty corner. Former captain Salman Akbar criticised the lack of preparation and organisation. This lapse raises serious questions about the team's readiness for major events.
briefs.bodyText:
Pakistan's 1-4 defeat to England in their opening Pool D match at the FIH Men's Hockey World Cup 2026 was compounded by an embarrassing moment involving captain Abu Bakar Mahmood, who was shown a green card after his team failed to produce the required protective gear for a penalty corner.
The bizarre incident in the 17th minute, shortly after England had taken a 1-0 lead, left former Pakistan captain Salman Akbar stunned. According to Akbar, Pakistan had forgotten the penalty-corner protective equipment in the changing room, forcing a player to sprint back to retrieve it.
The delay resulted in Abu Bakar being shown a green card and spending two minutes on the sidelines. For Akbar, the incident reflected a deeper problem with preparation and organisation at the highest level of the sport.
“Wow. Another unwanted record from Pakistan hockey. In the opening match of the FIH Hockey World Cup 2026 against England, Pakistan reportedly forgot the penalty corner protective gear in the changing room. As a result, the captain received the green card,” Akbar wrote on X.
‘Simply cannot happen on biggest stage’
Akbar was particularly critical of the fact that such an error occurred during a World Cup match, arguing that preparation extends well beyond tactics and physical fitness.
“Forgetting essential protective equipment for penalty corners simply cannot happen on the biggest stage of international hockey. Preparation is not just about tactics, fitness and skills. It is also about discipline and organisation,” the former captain wrote.
He added: “The World Cup demands the highest level of professionalism. Unfortunately, moments like this raise serious questions about how prepared we really are for the big stage.”
The incident came during a difficult outing for Pakistan, who eventually lost 1-4 to England. The defeat leaves them needing a strong response in their remaining Pool D matches, with India also part of the group.
